<a id="s0-p1"></a>[0¶1] This document is the contract for pcrec's generation-time tuning axes: every `-f`/`-fno-` flag, the value parameters `--unroll=K` and `--vm-entry-shape=N`, `--engine=` where it meets them, and the `--tune=N` dial. For each axis it states what the axis denies or forces, its default, the stamp an emitted artifact carries for it, whether `rx_info.flags` reflects it, and its class (§1). The value set of every stamp named here is `match_api.md` §6.3; the resource bounds are `limits.md`; the columns of `pcrec --list-axes` are `registry.md` §6. Design documents and decisions cited below are background, not part of the contract. The history of this document is `docs/dev/history/tuning_record.md`, which is not normative.

<a id="s0-p2"></a>[0¶2] Each axis's option bit is declared once, in `lib/pcrec.h`. Its CLI spellings and its default polarity are one row of `src/core/axes.def`, and every reader is derived from that row: the parser's whole `-f` grammar, and the `deny_macro`, `deny_bit`, `force_macro`, `force_bit` and `cli_flag` columns of `--list-axes`. A spelling in this document, in the listing and in the parser is therefore one fact.

<a id="s0-p3"></a>[0¶3] `pcrec --list-axes` is the machine-readable view of the axes: one row per (axis, candidate) for every bit-flag axis below, plus the DFA layer-1 axes (`table`, `prefilter`, `view`, `seed`, `accept`, `direction`; a candidate of these carries a flag only where a section below names one) and the first-match selection tables (`engine-route`, `fallback`, `prefilter-admit`, `req-admit`, `req-use`, `hyb-reseed`). It reports what this build's axes are; this document states what denying or forcing one does.

<a id="s1"></a>
## 1. What a tuning flag is

<a id="s1-p1"></a>[1¶1] A tuning flag is a generation-time choice (D18: options are compiled away, never a runtime parameter). It selects among machinery the compiler could otherwise choose on its own. Every axis belongs to one of four classes:

- <a id="s1-p2"></a>[1¶2] **ANSWER-IDENTICAL.** Denying or forcing the axis does not change what the emitted matcher answers for any subject: the span, every capture slot, and the failure surface (no-match, or a give-up and which one) are identical between the two builds under the default budgets. It changes how the answer is found, never the answer. Where an axis can move the give-up surface under a caller-tuned budget, its section says so and in which direction. Most axes are in this class.
- <a id="s1-p3"></a>[1¶3] **ENGINE-SELECTING.** Denying the axis leaves a DFA-excluding construct in the pattern, so a pattern that would compile to the DFA engine compiles to the VM instead, and `--engine=dfa` with the denial refuses. Answers are identical across the axis. §2.8, §2.9 and §2.44 are the engine-selecting denials `rx_info.flags` keeps (§2¶3); §2.32 moves the engine in the same way and is masked.
- <a id="s1-p4"></a>[1¶4] **CONTRACT.** The axis selects between ruled semantics, and the builds give different answers on one input class on purpose. §2.23 and §2.36.
- <a id="s1-p5"></a>[1¶5] **RENDERING.** §2.24 alone: it changes the emitted comments and nothing a compiler sees.

> <a id="s1-p6"></a>[1¶6] **The answer-identity rule.** Denying (or forcing) a tuning axis that is not a CONTRACT axis must not change what the emitted matcher answers for any subject.

<a id="s1-p7"></a>[1¶7] The rule is D46's principle (every strategy-selection point is observable and forceable) applied at the tuning layer: a strategy that cannot be denied cannot be differentially tested (D47.3). An axis's section names the differential that compares the two builds where one exists.

<a id="s1-p8"></a>[1¶8] `--tune=N` (§5) is a profile: one option that sets a group of axes from a pinned table. An axis's default in §2 is its value at `--tune=0` (`balanced`), and §5.4 gives its value at the other four positions. The dial changes an axis only where §5.4 has a cell for it.

<a id="s1-p9"></a>[1¶9] An explicit per-axis flag beats the dial wherever a spelling exists. Two kinds of dial cell have no spelling that could override them: a deny-only axis the dial denies has no force twin (`-fno-premul-table` at `−2`), and the `[ART-SIZE]` ladder's two parameters (§2.16) have no CLI spelling at all — the materiality bar is the `limits.def` row `PCREC_SIZE_TERM_BAR` and the threshold is `PCREC_SIZE_TERM_THRESHOLD`, which only a `-D` at pcrec's build moves (`limits.md` §8b).

<a id="s1-p10"></a>[1¶10] Where an axis has both a deny and a force spelling, passing both is not an override. `-fprefilter` with `-fno-prefilter`, `-fprefilter-collapse` with `-fno-prefilter-collapse`, and `-fstartpos-guard=align` with `-fno-startpos-guard` are refused as a pair. `-fcomments` with `-fno-comments` and `-fmemfn-simd` with `-fno-memfn-simd` compile, and the deny spelling wins.

<a id="s2"></a>
## 2. The axes

<a id="s2-p1"></a>[2¶1] Each subsection states what the axis controls, its default, the stamp it leaves in an emitted artifact, its class (§1), how `rx_info.flags` treats it, the differential that compares the two builds where one exists, and its place on the dial (§5.4).

<a id="s2-p2"></a>[2¶2] `make test-axes` (`tests/axes/run_axes.sh`) enforces every answer-identity promise below: the whole `.rxt` corpus, case by case, under every deny and force spelling `--list-axes` carries and under `--engine=`, compared against the default build. It classifies a documented refusal (§2.3's replication cap, §2.5's forced-prefilter refusal, §2.33's denied-kit size refusal) and a budget boundary moving (a give-up or a per-case timeout on either side) separately from an answer disagreement; `docs/testing.md`, "Answer-identity sweep", says how to read a failure. `-futf-check` is excluded from the identity sweep by name and has its own arm (§2.36).

<a id="s2-p3"></a>[2¶3] **The `rx_info.flags` rule.** Every axis bit `src/core/axes.def` names is masked out of `rx_info.flags`, on every artifact, whether or not the axis could act on it, except the bits in a fixed KEPT set: the three engine-selecting denials `PCREC_NO_ATOMIC_DISCHARGE`, `PCREC_NO_SPLICE_CALLS` and `PCREC_NO_POSS_CTX_FOLLOW` (§2.8, §2.9, §2.44), and the contract bits `PCREC_NO_STARTPOS_GUARD`, `PCREC_FORCE_STARTPOS_ALIGN` and `PCREC_FORCE_UTF_CHECK` (§2.23, §2.36), which are masked only under the `byte` encoding, where they are inert. `PCREC_SIZE_CAP_REFUSE` (`--size-cap=refuse`, `limits.md` §8.4) is not an axis row and is masked too. The mask is derived from the axis table with "masked" as the default (`emit_info_def`, `src/gen/emit_dfa.c`), so a new axis is masked from the day it is added. A masked axis changes no answer, so two artifacts that behave identically do not differ in their reflection surface over it; what the emitter did is recorded in the stamp its section names. `tests/codegen/run_prechecks.sh` section 6b checks every `-f` spelling `--list-axes` carries against this rule.

<a id="s2-1"></a>
### 2.1 `-fno-possessify` — `PCREC_NO_POSSESSIFY` (bit 4)

<a id="s2-1-p1"></a>[2.1¶1] **Denies** the possessification rewrite (`src/opt/possessify.c`; design `docs/design/eng_brep_design.md` §2): a quantifier whose loop cannot give back a character the continuation needs is emitted possessive. Default: the rewrite runs. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`.

<a id="s2-1-p2"></a>[2.1¶2] **The stamp** is the `<PREFIX>_VM_STRATS` bitmask: `PCREC_VM_STRAT_POSSESSIVE` (`0x1`) where some quantifier possessified and `PCREC_VM_STRAT_BACKTRACKING` (`0x2`) where some quantifier kept its backtracking loop (`lib/pcrec.h`'s shared ABI block names the bits; the emitted line carries only the hex value). `.frame_capacity` can grow under the denial, because a backtracking loop needs a resume frame a possessive one does not (`match_api.md` §6¶16).

<a id="s2-1-p3"></a>[2.1¶3] **The give-up surface moves under a caller-tuned budget, in two directions.** A possessified loop keeps no resume frames and spends no backtrack steps on retreats, so a `PCREC_ERR_STEPS` or `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` give-up of the denied build can become an answer. Its forward scan is charged to the work budget per iteration, so a `PCREC_ERR_WORK` give-up can appear where the denied build answered (`limits.md` §7). Under the default budgets the answers are identical. The arms of §2.44 and §2.45 widen which loops possessify, and so widen both effects.

<a id="s2-1-p4"></a>[2.1¶4] **Differential:** `tests/possessify/run_possdiff.sh` (pcrec against pcrec, the axis denied against the default, one driver comparing span, every capture slot and the failure surface over every subject and start position).

<a id="s2-1-p5"></a>[2.1¶5] **Dial:** no cell, GATE 3 (§5.4).

<a id="s2-2"></a>
### 2.2 `-fno-revdet` — `PCREC_NO_REVDET` (bit 5)

<a id="s2-2-p1"></a>[2.2¶1] **Denies** the REVERSE-DETERMINISTIC cursor rung (`docs/design/engine_m4.md` §2.5): a quantifier that would take the rung drops one rung further, to literal replication with frames. Default: the rung runs where it applies. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. **The stamp** is the `<PREFIX>_VM_RUNGS` bitmask's `PCREC_VM_RUNG_REVDET` bit.

<a id="s2-2-p2"></a>[2.2¶2] **Differential:** `tests/rungselect/run_rungdiff.sh`, on the shared driver of §2.1.

<a id="s2-2-p3"></a>[2.2¶3] **Dial:** no cell, GATE 3 (§5.4).

<a id="s2-3"></a>
### 2.3 `-fno-counter` — `PCREC_NO_COUNTER` (bit 6)

<a id="s2-3-p1"></a>[2.3¶1] **Denies** the COUNTER rung (`docs/design/counterk_impl/counterk_design.md`): a bounded repeat that would take it drops to literal replication. Default: the rung runs where it applies, unrolled by `K` (§2.10). ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. **The stamp** is the `<PREFIX>_VM_RUNGS` bitmask's `PCREC_VM_RUNG_COUNTER` bit.

<a id="s2-3-p2"></a>[2.3¶2] **Its denial has a limit.** Literal replication is capped at `PCREC_MAX_VM_REPEAT_COPIES` copies of one repeat's body (`limits.md` §3.3), so a repeat above the cap compiles with the counter rung and is refused under the denial. `make test-axes` records that refusal as this axis's documented limit. Below the cap, the replicated build is the counter rung's only ground truth: no third strategy sits under it.

<a id="s2-3-p3"></a>[2.3¶3] **Differential:** `tests/counterk/run_counterkdiff.sh`, on the shared driver of §2.1.

<a id="s2-3-p4"></a>[2.3¶4] **Dial:** no cell, NOT A RUNG: the rung is the floor the ladder's other rungs are checked against, not a size or speed lever (§5.4).

<a id="s2-4"></a>
### 2.4 `-fno-length-prune` — `PCREC_NO_LENGTH_PRUNE` (bit 7)

<a id="s2-4-p1"></a>[2.4¶1] **Denies** MINIMUM-REMAINING-LENGTH (MRL) pruning (`docs/design/k23_impl/k23_design.md`, D51): a bound, emitted on whichever rung a quantifier took, that abandons a loop iteration once the subject left is too short for the rest of the pattern. Default: MRL prunes where a bound is derivable. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. It changes no rung, no slot and no capacity, so the denied artifact is the emitter's program without the bounds. **The stamp** is the `<PREFIX>_VM_PRUNES` bitmask (`PCREC_VM_PRUNE_CLAMPED` / `PCREC_VM_PRUNE_UNCLAMPED`), beside `<PREFIX>_VM_PRUNE_CEILING`, the ceiling the bounds are measured against.

<a id="s2-4-p2"></a>[2.4¶2] **Differential:** `tests/mrl/run_mrldiff.sh`, on the shared driver of §2.1, over both engines: the default route's prefilter-windowed ceiling and `--engine=vm`'s subject-end ceiling are different arithmetic, so both run.

<a id="s2-4-p3"></a>[2.4¶3] **Dial:** no cell, NOT A RUNG: MRL trades nothing (§5.4).

<a id="s2-5"></a>
### 2.5 `-fno-prefilter` / `-fprefilter` — `PCREC_NO_PREFILTER` (bit 8) / `PCREC_FORCE_PREFILTER` (bit 9)

<a id="s2-5-p1"></a>[2.5¶1] **Controls** whether a VM artifact runs the HYBRID PREFILTER: a capture-erased DFA, inlined as `static <prefix>_prefilter`, that runs ahead of the VM program and hands it candidate windows (`fit.prefilter`, `src/opt/select_engine.c`; design `docs/design/engine_m4.md` §6.1, §4.7). It is one verdict for the whole artifact, decided jointly with the engine, so the axis is a FORCE PAIR: `-fno-prefilter` asks for the OFF state under `auto`, and `-fprefilter` for the ON state under `--engine=vm`. Default: selected with the engine — `auto` turns it on for a VM-routed pattern the prefilter admits (the `prefilter-admit` axis of `--list-axes`), and `--engine=vm` turns it off.

<a id="s2-5-p2"></a>[2.5¶2] ANSWER-IDENTICAL in one direction and DO-OR-DIE in the other. `-fno-prefilter` never refuses: `--engine=vm` already ships that configuration. `-fprefilter` on a pattern that compiles to the DFA engine refuses with a diagnostic, because there is no VM artifact to attach a prefilter to. Both bits are masked out of `rx_info.flags`. **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER`, `"hybrid"` or `"none"`; a hybrid also carries the DFA scan's own stamps (§3.1).

<a id="s2-5-p3"></a>[2.5¶3] **`-fprefilter` is charged against the emitted-size caps and never dropped to fit.** The forced prefilter's DFA counts toward `limits.md` §8's caps, so a pattern that fits without it can be refused with it, with the size-cap diagnostic. The size-cap ladder's rungs that would drop the prefilter are not offered under this flag (§2.17). `make test-axes` records that refusal as the axis's documented limit.

<a id="s2-5-p4"></a>[2.5¶4] **Identity is modulo which budget binds.** The prefilter changes how much work a search does before it answers, and a give-up is a bound on work, so on a subject near a budget the two builds can differ by a give-up code where neither is wrong (`((a)|bc){0,4000}d` over 1 MB of `a` is no match with the prefilter and `PCREC_ERR_WORK` without it). A sweep across this axis classifies a give-up on either side as budget-bound, not as a disagreement.

<a id="s2-5-p5"></a>[2.5¶5] **Two routes turn the prefilter off without the flag**, and neither claims the flag's credit:

- <a id="s2-5-p6"></a>[2.5¶6] a DFA-cap overflow under `auto`. With neither `-fprefilter` nor `-fno-prefilter` requested, an auto-selected prefilter whose own DFA build overflows a cap (state count, table entries, the subset-element budget) is dropped rather than refused, after the collapse rung of §2.17 has been tried: the artifact stamps `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none"`, and `--emit-ir`'s `prefilter` summary row reads `no-dfa-overflow` (`ir_listing.md` §3.1.1);
- <a id="s2-5-p7"></a>[2.5¶7] the size-cap ladder's prefilter drop (`limits.md` §8.4). A hybrid whose artifact is over an emitted-size cap after the §2.17 collapse has its prefilter dropped and stamps `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none"` with `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_WHY "size cap retry, hybrid N > CAP"`, the one `"none"` that stamp is written beside; `--emit-ir` reads `no-size-cap`. Never under `-fprefilter`, where the compile refuses instead, and denied with the other slower-to-fit rungs by `--size-cap=refuse`.

<a id="s2-5-p8"></a>[2.5¶8] `-fprefilter` is unchanged by either route: forcing the prefilter on a pattern whose DFA cannot be built refuses with the DFA overflow diagnostic (§2.11).

<a id="s2-5-p9"></a>[2.5¶9] **Differential:** none of its own. That the hybrid answers the span the pure VM would rides `tests/vm/run_vm_tests.sh` §3.7 and the ceiling-form coverage of `tests/mrl/run_mrl_tests.sh`; `tests/prefilter/run_prefilter_tests.sh` pairs the stamp with an independent read of the emitted `_prefilter(` bodies.

<a id="s2-5-p10"></a>[2.5¶10] **Dial:** no cell, GATE 3 (§5.4).

<a id="s2-6"></a>
### 2.6 `-fno-altcls-merge` — `PCREC_NO_ALTCLS_MERGE` (bit 10)

<a id="s2-6-p1"></a>[2.6¶1] **Denies** stage 1 of the alternation-to-class pass (`src/opt/altcls.c`): merging a maximal run of single-character alternation branches into one class. Default: stage 1 runs where a run qualifies. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Each mergeable run is its own selection point, so the axis is deny-only. The pass runs before either engine is built, so it is not VM-only: a DFA artifact carries its stamp too. **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_ALTCLS_MERGES`, a count.

<a id="s2-6-p2"></a>[2.6¶2] **Its denial moves the refusal set.** A nested repeat whose replicated size fits only after the merge (`tests/size/size_term.rxt`'s nested-repeat tower) is refused under the denial (K45).

<a id="s2-6-p3"></a>[2.6¶3] **Differential:** `tests/altcls/run_altdiff.sh`, which denies both stages together (§2.7).

<a id="s2-6-p4"></a>[2.6¶4] **Dial:** no cell: wrong-signed (denying the merge costs bytes) and GATE 2 (§5.4).

<a id="s2-7"></a>
### 2.7 `-fno-altcls-factor` — `PCREC_NO_ALTCLS_FACTOR` (bit 11)

<a id="s2-7-p1"></a>[2.7¶1] **Denies** stage 2 of the same pass: prefix-factoring a maximal run of branches that share a literal first byte. Stage 2 runs on stage 1's output, so denying stage 1 alone still lets stage 2 factor an unmerged run's literal spelling, and denying stage 2 alone leaves single-character merging live. Default: stage 2 runs where a run qualifies. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`, not VM-only. **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_ALTCLS_FACTORED`, a count.

<a id="s2-7-p2"></a>[2.7¶2] **Differential:** `tests/altcls/run_altdiff.sh` (both stages denied against both live, on the shared driver of §2.1).

<a id="s2-7-p3"></a>[2.7¶3] **Dial:** no cell: wrong-signed (§5.4).

<a id="s2-8"></a>
### 2.8 `-fno-atomic-discharge` — `PCREC_NO_ATOMIC_DISCHARGE` (bit 12)

<a id="s2-8-p1"></a>[2.8¶1] **Denies** the FREE DISCHARGE (`src/opt/atomic.c`; design `docs/design/atomic_groups_design.md` §5.3): deleting an atomic group, or a possessive quantifier's atomic suffix, whose cut the possessify verdict proves is a no-op. Default: the discharge runs where it is provably safe. It is not gated by `-fno-possessify`: an optimization denial does not decide which engine a pattern gets.

<a id="s2-8-p2"></a>[2.8¶2] ENGINE-SELECTING, KEPT in `rx_info.flags`. An undischarged atomic group is DFA-excluding, so under the denial a pattern that would compile to the DFA compiles to the VM, and `--engine=dfa` with the denial refuses with the construct's diagnostic (`possessive quantifier requires the VM engine, which --engine=dfa excludes`, on `[^"]*+"` with `--no-captures`). No stamp of its own: `<PREFIX>_ENGINE` is the observable consequence.

<a id="s2-8-p3"></a>[2.8¶3] The discharge asks the possessify verdict, so the arms of §2.44 and §2.45 widen what it discharges: `\w++\b` is discharged and routed to the DFA by default, and denying §2.44 keeps it on the VM.

<a id="s2-8-p4"></a>[2.8¶4] **Differential:** `tests/atomic_groups/run_atomic_diff.sh` §3, pcrec against pcrec with and without the flag, beside that suite's sweeps against libpcre2.

<a id="s2-8-p5"></a>[2.8¶5] **Dial:** no cell, GATE 3 (§5.4).

<a id="s2-9"></a>
### 2.9 `-fno-splice-calls` — `PCREC_NO_SPLICE_CALLS` (bit 13)

<a id="s2-9-p1"></a>[2.9¶1] **Denies** the SPLICE linkage at every eligible subroutine call site (design `docs/design/subroutines_design.md` §6.3, §9.2), forcing the CALL linkage everywhere. Default: a call site whose callee is not in a cycle and whose expansion fits the splice budget (`PCREC_MAX_SPLICE_NODES`, `PCREC_MAX_SPLICE_TOTAL`) is spliced, emitted inline as its own copy; every other site takes the shared CALL linkage.

<a id="s2-9-p2"></a>[2.9¶2] ENGINE-SELECTING, KEPT in `rx_info.flags`. A spliced call has an exact finite lowering, so the DFA can be built; a linked call is VM-only. Under the denial `--engine=dfa` refuses (`(?&name) requires the VM engine, which --engine=dfa excludes`, on `(?:(?<g>a)){0}(?&g)` with `--no-captures`), and an `--emit-main` build of `(a)(?1)` carries `.flags = 8194ULL` under the flag against `.flags = 2ULL` without it (`PCREC_EMIT_MAIN` plus bit 13).

<a id="s2-9-p3"></a>[2.9¶3] **The stamp** is two counts, `<PREFIX>_VM_CALL_SPLICED` and `<PREFIX>_VM_CALL_LINKED`: their sum is every call site the emitter wrote. On `(a)(?1)` they read `1`/`0` by default and `0`/`1` under the flag.

<a id="s2-9-p4"></a>[2.9¶4] **Differential:** `tests/recursion/run_recursion_diff.sh` §5 ("`A == B`"), the spliced and the linked artifact compared on answers over the corpus. `tests/codegen/run_recursion_identity.sh` is the separate byte-identity gate for the module-boundary claim.

<a id="s2-9-p5"></a>[2.9¶5] **Dial:** no cell, GATE 4 (§5.4).

<a id="s2-10"></a>
### 2.10 `--unroll=K` — the counter rung's value parameter

<a id="s2-10-p1"></a>[2.10¶1] Not a bit of `pcrec_options.flags`: the separate field `unroll_k`. The counter rung (§2.3) emits one body copy per `K` iterations plus a trailed counter that makes the realized iteration count exact at any `K >= 1`. `K = 0` in the field means the built-in default `PCREC_DEFAULT_UNROLL_K` (`limits.md` §8a). The CLI accepts an integer in `1..4096`. One value per artifact, never per quantifier.

<a id="s2-10-p2"></a>[2.10¶2] ANSWER-IDENTICAL in the language, not in the depth. A smaller `K` raises the per-iteration frame need, so the same capacity carries a shorter subject (`^(a(?1)?b)$`'s `.subject_ceiling` is 512 at `--unroll=8` and 341 at `--unroll=1`); `limits.md` §8a states the rule and the numbers. **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K`, beside `<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY`, whose `option` value records an explicit `--unroll` (§2.16).

<a id="s2-10-p3"></a>[2.10¶3] **The dial never sets `K`.** `--tune=N` moves the size-term ladder's bar and threshold (§2.16), and the ladder derives `K` per pattern from them. The ladder's declared-capacity floor is a precondition of both size-side dial cells: a candidate `K` whose artifact declares less capacity than the default `K`'s — on `.frame_capacity` or on `.subject_ceiling` — is not a candidate, and the artifact stamps `capacity-declined` (design `docs/design/artifact_size_term.md` §3.3a). Without the floor a lower threshold would turn a match into a give-up.

<a id="s2-11"></a>
### 2.11 `--engine=dfa|vm|auto` — the engine request

<a id="s2-11-p1"></a>[2.11¶1] Not a `-f` flag; it is the coarsest selection the engine-selecting axes (§1) also reach. Default: `auto`, the per-pattern selection (APPROACH.md §2). `dfa` and `vm` are diagnostic overrides, and DO-OR-DIE: a request the pattern cannot honour refuses with a diagnostic naming the construct, never a silent fallback (`src/opt/select_engine.c`). `--engine=vm` also turns the hybrid prefilter off unless `-fprefilter` is passed (§2.5), which is what makes a `--engine=vm` build an independent derivation of the span. **The stamps** are `<PREFIX>_ENGINE` (`"dfa"` or `"vm"`), `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_WHY` on a VM artifact (the construct that forced the VM), and `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL` (the route the selection took, §2.17's attribution order). `PCREC_ENGINE_AUTO` is an enum member of `lib/pcrec.h`; `PCREC_ENGINE_DFA` and `PCREC_ENGINE_VM` are `#define`s, so an artifact's own identical `#define` of the same name does not collide with the header.

<a id="s2-11-p2"></a>[2.11¶2] **Forcing the VM can turn a match into a give-up.** A DFA has no per-nesting-level frame cost; the VM's resume stack and trail are consumed at about two frames and nine trail entries per nesting level whatever the subject length (`limits.md` §4). A pattern nested deeply enough matches a one-byte subject under `auto` (on the DFA) and gives up `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` under `--engine=vm`: `tests/base/k18_deep_nesting.rxt` is the witness (K18).

<a id="s2-11-p3"></a>[2.11¶3] **`auto`'s one exception to do-or-die is a DFA cap.** Every other refusal is decided from the pattern before an automaton is built. A DFA-cap overflow (state count, table entries, the subset-element budget, `limits.md` §3.3) is found only by attempting the build, and under `auto` — with neither `--engine=dfa` nor `-fprefilter` — it is a selection outcome: the compile falls back to the VM (`<PREFIX>_ENGINE "vm"`, `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_WHY` naming the cap, `"dfa overflowed: >N states at pattern offset 0"`), and a VM-routed pattern whose auto-selected prefilter's DFA overflowed has the prefilter dropped or collapsed (§2.5, §2.17). `--engine=dfa` and `-fprefilter` still refuse, with `pattern too complex for the DFA engine (>N states; try --engine=vm)`.

<a id="s2-11-p4"></a>[2.11¶4] The fallback compile reruns the pipeline with the DFA excluded from selection outright (`Ctx.dfa_disabled`, read by `select_engine.c`'s `forces_dfa_overflow` row and by the prefilter derivation in one step), so the overflowing machine is never built twice. Its cost is at most two refused DFA builds more than asking for `--engine=vm`: the exact machine, and the count-collapsed prefilter's (§2.17), which is strictly smaller; `-fno-prefilter-collapse` removes the second. The `RX_ENGINE_WHY` text carries the usual `" at pattern offset N"` suffix with offset 0. If a real construct also forces the VM, that construct's reason wins `RX_ENGINE_WHY` (first wins); the overflow's effect on the prefilter applies independently. Witness: `tests/vm/run_vm_tests.sh` §3b.

<a id="s2-11-p5"></a>[2.11¶5] **A fallback ships a VM artifact that a DFA refusal would not have produced**, so only the VM emitter's own bounds apply to it: `PCREC_MAX_VM_NODES`, `PCREC_MAX_VM_REPEAT_COPIES`, `PCREC_MAX_VM_REPLICATION_PRODUCT` and the emitted-size caps (`limits.md` §3.3, §8). Such an artifact can be large enough that compiling it with gcc is itself expensive (K41).

<a id="s2-11-p6"></a>[2.11¶6] **Differential:** none of its own: every module's differential sweeps at least the default and `--engine=vm` builds (`tests/atomic_groups/run_atomic_diff.sh` §2, `tests/recursion/run_recursion_diff.sh`).

<a id="s2-11-p7"></a>[2.11¶7] **Dial:** no cell, GATE 5 and GATE 2 (§5.4).

<a id="s2-12"></a>
### 2.12 `-fno-tiered-entry` — `PCREC_NO_TIERED_ENTRY` (bit 14)

<a id="s2-12-p1"></a>[2.12¶1] **Denies** the two-tier entry. On an artifact whose stamped default storage does not fit inside one 4 KB page, `<prefix>_search`, `_match` and `_match_caps` run the match on a page-budgeted on-stack buffer first and escalate to the stamped default — by calling a non-inlined internal function that owns it and re-runs the match from scratch — on `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` and on nothing else (`match_api.md` §10.9, `limits.md` §3.2). Under the denial the entries run single-tier. Default: the tier is on. Deny-only: one entry shape per artifact.

<a id="s2-12-p2"></a>[2.12¶2] ANSWER-IDENTICAL by construction: the two shapes answer identically, and a give-up always means the stamped default ran out. Masked out of `rx_info.flags`. **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_FAST_FRAMES` / `<PREFIX>_FAST_TRAIL` (`match_api.md` §6.3), VM-only and `.c`-private, on every VM artifact. Under the denial they equal `<PREFIX>_RESUME_FRAMES` / `<PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAMES`, and FAST equal to RESUME/TRAIL is how a reader tells that an artifact has one tier (degenerate artifacts read that way too). Grep for `^#define RX_FAST_`: a looser `RX_(FAST|RESUME|TRAIL)` also matches the sizing macros of `match_api.md` §10.4 and the `RX_TRAIL` undo macro.

<a id="s2-12-p3"></a>[2.12¶3] **Differential:** `tests/codegen/run_tiered_entry.sh` §5 compares the tiered artifact with the denied one.

<a id="s2-12-p4"></a>[2.12¶4] **Dial:** no cell today; conditional at `−2` and `−1` pending an unmeasured quantity (§5.4).

<a id="s2-13"></a>
### 2.13 `-fno-premul-table` — `PCREC_NO_PREMUL_TABLE` (bit 15)

<a id="s2-13-p1"></a>[2.13¶1] **Denies** the PRE-MULTIPLIED transition table. A DFA scan's table normally holds `next_state * classes` rather than `next_state`, so the emitted step is `state = table[state + class]` over 16-bit cells with `65535` for dead; denied, it emits the INDEXED form, `table[state * classes + class]`. The same states, byte classes and transitions are written down differently. Default: pre-multiplied, subject to the bound below. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only. Design: `docs/design/premultiplied_dfa_table.md`.

<a id="s2-13-p2"></a>[2.13¶2] **The bound is not this flag.** The pre-multiplied form is declined per machine, at generation time, when the machine's `states * classes` exceeds 65,535 or an emitted seed cell would be negative: a cell must fit 16 bits and stay distinguishable from the dead sentinel. It is a correctness condition, not a budget, and declining it never refuses a pattern. The forward, reverse and anchored machines decide separately, which is why `"mixed"` exists.

<a id="s2-13-p3"></a>[2.13¶3] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE` (§3), on every artifact that contains a DFA scan: `"premultiplied"`, `"indexed"`, `"mixed"` (the machines disagree) or `"none"` (no numeric table: an `attempt` or `empty` scan).

<a id="s2-13-p4"></a>[2.13¶4] **pcrec may set this axis itself on a size-cap refusal.** The size-cap ladder's `drop-premul` rung (`limits.md` §8.4; `--list-axes` axis `fallback`) denies this axis for a DFA-engine artifact's retry, tried after §2.15's `drop-anchored` rung when that one did not clear the cap. The retry stamps `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "size-cap-retry"` and `<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE` off `"premultiplied"`, and a non-fatal stderr note names the drop and points at `--max-emit-bytes` / `--max-emit-code-bytes`. A VM hybrid's prefilter table has no such rung.

<a id="s2-13-p5"></a>[2.13¶5] **Dial:** `−2` denies it; `−1` is conditional, pending an unmeasured quantity (§5.4).

<a id="s2-14"></a>
### 2.14 `-fno-offset-skip` — `PCREC_NO_OFFSET_SKIP` (bit 16)

<a id="s2-14-p1"></a>[2.14¶1] **Denies** the OFFSET-SET candidate filter. A DFA artifact's forward scan filters candidate match starts on the byte at the candidate (one `memchr` for a single value, a 256-entry bitmap walk for a set). With this axis on, the compiler may instead derive from the pattern's prefix a set of `(offset k, byte-set)` tests every match must satisfy — for `\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}`, a digit at offset 0 and a `-` at offset 4 — scan for the rarest member at its offset, verify the others on each candidate, and resume one position after a failed candidate. Every test is a necessary condition of a match beginning there. Default: on, subject to the selection below. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only. Design: `docs/design/offset_k_skip.md`.

<a id="s2-14-p2"></a>[2.14¶2] **The selection is not this flag.** The form is adopted only where a cost model over the compile's byte-rate (`findings.md`) predicts it at least twice as cheap as the offset-0 filter (`src/opt/prefix_k.c`), and the scan offset holds a single byte value unless it is offset 0. Offset 0 is always a member of the set. The set holds at most `PCREC_OFSK_MAX_SET` offsets and the walk looks at most `PCREC_PREFIX_K_MAX` offsets deep; exceeding either declines the form and never refuses a pattern.

<a id="s2-14-p3"></a>[2.14¶3] **The stamps.** `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER` reads `"offset-set"` or `"offset-set-bounded"`, and `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS` names the chosen offsets with `*` on the scanned one (`"0,4*"`), `"none"` on every other artifact. The denial also removes the run-pinned rows of §2.30, which emit the same block. On `\b[0-9a-f]{32}\b` the selection declines without the flag (`"byte-class-bounded"` / `"none"`).

<a id="s2-14-p4"></a>[2.14¶4] **Dial:** no cell: flat, below the dial's materiality bar (§5.4).

<a id="s2-15"></a>
### 2.15 `-fno-anchored-dfa` — `PCREC_NO_ANCHORED_DFA` (bit 17)

<a id="s2-15-p1"></a>[2.15¶1] **Denies** the ANCHORED MACHINE behind `<prefix>_match` and `<prefix>_match_caps` on a DFA artifact. With the axis on, the artifact carries a third machine — the same subset construction over the same NFA, rooted at the pattern's own first state instead of the start-anywhere self-loop — and runs it forward from `ctx->pos`, with no reverse pass and no candidate skip. Denied, those entries run the artifact's unanchored search and reject a match whose start is not `ctx->pos`, and no third machine is built. Default: on, subject to the selection below. ANSWER-IDENTICAL (`match_api.md` §3.2; the argument is `docs/design/anchored_match_unwrapped.md` §3), masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only.

<a id="s2-15-p2"></a>[2.15¶2] **The selection is not this flag.** The anchored form needs the one-pass unanchored DFA engine (a `^`- or `\G`-bearing pattern runs on the per-start `attempt` scan and keeps the search-filter form), an artifact that is not the empty engine, and an anchored machine that builds inside the DFA caps (`PCREC_ANCHORED_MAX_STATES`, and the shared caps after the mandatory machines are built). A machine over a cap declines the form; it never refuses a pattern.

<a id="s2-15-p3"></a>[2.15¶3] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH`, `"unwrapped"` or `"search-filter"`, mirrored at run time by `rx_info.match_form` (§3). On `^foo` the selection declines without the flag (`RX_DFA_SCAN "attempt"`, `RX_DFA_MATCH "search-filter"`).

<a id="s2-15-p4"></a>[2.15¶4] **pcrec may set this axis itself on a size-cap refusal.** The anchored machine is optional, but its bytes count toward the emitted-size caps. On a size-cap refusal with the machine present, the ladder's `drop-anchored` rung (`limits.md` §8.4) drops it and re-emits; the artifact is the one this flag produces plus `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "size-cap-retry"`, which tells "pcrec dropped it to fit" apart from "the caller passed the flag" (`"selected"`). If the cap still refuses, §2.13's `drop-premul` rung follows; an artifact whose retry fired both reads `RX_DFA_MATCH "search-filter"` and `RX_DFA_TABLE` off `"premultiplied"`. Passing the flag still denies the machine unconditionally.

<a id="s2-15-p5"></a>[2.15¶5] **Dial:** no cell, deliberately excluded from `−2` pending its own measurement (§5.4).

<a id="s2-16"></a>
### 2.16 `-fno-size-term` — `PCREC_NO_SIZE_TERM` (bit 18)

<a id="s2-16-p1"></a>[2.16¶1] **Denies** the SIZE TERM: on an artifact whose counter rung (§2.3) is live and whose emitted size exceeds the threshold, `K` is chosen by re-emitting a descending ladder of unroll factors and taking the smallest emitted node count, kept only where it saves at least the materiality bar's share of the bytes. Denied, `K` stays `--unroll=K` or `PCREC_DEFAULT_UNROLL_K`. Default: on, with the bar `PCREC_SIZE_TERM_BAR` (75, so a 25% saving) and the threshold `PCREC_SIZE_TERM_THRESHOLD` (120,000 bytes) at `--tune=0`; §5.4 moves both. Masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Design: `docs/design/artifact_size_term.md`.

<a id="s2-16-p2"></a>[2.16¶2] **ANSWER-IDENTICAL for matches and captures, not for the give-up surface.** The span and the capture slots are identical at every `K`. What the artifact gives up on is not: on `((a)|ab){12}c` the least `--step-budget` that completes is 89 at `K = 1` and 110 at `K = 8`, the least `--backtrack-frames` is 39 at `K = 1` and 28 at `K = 8`, and `<PREFIX>_TRAIL_FRAMES` runs from 62 to 51. Under the default budgets the answers are identical (`limits.md` §7).

<a id="s2-16-p3"></a>[2.16¶3] **It does not control the emitted-size caps.** The denial removes the mechanism that would have made the artifact smaller; it never reaches `PCREC_MAX_VM_EMIT_CODE_BYTES` or `PCREC_MAX_EMIT_BYTES`, so a denied build can still be refused for size. To accept a larger artifact, raise a cap (`--max-emit-bytes=N`, `--max-emit-code-bytes=N`, `limits.md` §8.6).

<a id="s2-16-p4"></a>[2.16¶4] **The stamps** are `<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K` (the chosen `K`) and `<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY`, both on every VM artifact. `<PREFIX>_UNROLL_K_WHY` has seven values, and names the first of them, in this order, whose condition holds: `option` (an explicit `--unroll`), `denied` (this flag), `default`, `cap-rescue`, `size-model`, `capacity-declined` (§2.10's floor removed every smaller candidate), `size-model-declined`. So `--unroll=K` reads `option` even under `-fno-size-term`, and the flag reads `denied` even where the counter rung is not live. `--list-axes` lists the `size-term` axis in the same order.

<a id="s2-16-p5"></a>[2.16¶5] **Dial:** the flag itself has no cell (NOT A RUNG); the mechanism's two parameters do (§5.4):

| `--tune=` | materiality bar | threshold (bytes) |
|---|---:|---:|
| `-2` `min-size` | 0.95 (saves at least 5%) | 40,000 |
| `-1` `size` | 0.85 (saves at least 15%) | 80,000 |
| `0` `balanced` | 0.75 (saves at least 25%) | 120,000 |
| `+1` / `+2` | — | — |

<a id="s2-17"></a>
### 2.17 `-fno-prefilter-collapse` / `-fprefilter-collapse` — `PCREC_NO_PREFILTER_COLLAPSE` (bit 19) / `PCREC_FORCE_PREFILTER_COLLAPSE` (bit 20)

<a id="s2-17-p1"></a>[2.17¶1] **Controls** which LANGUAGE the hybrid prefilter's DFA (§2.5) recognises. The default builds it from the pattern's own language (`"exact"`). The COUNT-COLLAPSED superset lowers every repeat with `rmin > 1` or `rmax > 1` as `X{min(rmin,1),}`, so the machine and the artifact stop growing with the count. The prefilter is a filter — it owes the VM a sound rejection and a lower bound on the match start, both of which a superset supplies, and the VM re-derives the answer from every candidate (`match_api.md` §6.3.5¶4) — so the axis is ANSWER-IDENTICAL in both directions at an unbounded budget. Both bits are masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Design: `docs/design/prefilter_count_independence.md`.

<a id="s2-17-p2"></a>[2.17¶2] **Where the collapse is used by default.** Only as an attempt on the compile's fallback ladder, where the exact machine cannot be built or its artifact cannot ship:

| rung | trigger | `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG_WHY` |
|---|---|---|
| DFA overflow (`fallback` row `sel1-collapse`) | a DFA cap overflowed while building the exact prefilter, so the alternative is no prefilter | `dfa overflow retry, exact nfa N` |
| size cap (`fallback` row `prefilter-collapse`) | an emitted-size cap refused the exact artifact, so the alternative is the ladder's next row | `size cap retry, exact N > cap` |

<a id="s2-17-p3"></a>[2.17¶3] The ladder takes the first row, in the `fallback` axis's order in `--list-axes`, that applies to the arrival and is not denied. No state-count threshold triggers the collapse: the emitted-size caps and the DFA caps are the only quantities that decide.

<a id="s2-17-p4"></a>[2.17¶4] **Attribution.** `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL` names the latest fired row that attributes the outcome, tested in this order (the `engine-route` axis of `--list-axes`): `forced`, `declined-nullable-default`, `declined-nullable`, `collapsed-prefilter`, `overflowed-dfa`, `overflowed-prefilter`, `size-cap-retry`, `selected`.

<a id="s2-17-p5"></a>[2.17¶5] **A prefilter is declined where the pattern admits an unconfined empty match.** A filter that matches the empty string at every position can dismiss none, so pcrec builds no prefilter for such a language: the artifact stamps `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none"`. The test is the pattern-facts record's `empty_admits` (`facts_listing.md`): some way of matching the empty string crosses no non-multiline `^`/`\A` or no non-multiline `$`/`\Z`/`\z`. A nullable pattern whose every empty path crosses both (`^(\s+)*$`, `\A(a*)*\z`) keeps its exact prefilter (`"selected"`, `"hybrid"`); one-sided and multiline forms are declined. Every other zero-width construct counts as always satisfiable, so the answer errs only toward declining. A `${...}` pattern is never declined: its variable turns the prefilter off first (`--emit-ir` `no-variable`, `"selected"`). The decline applies:

- <a id="s2-17-p6"></a>[2.17¶6] to an ordinary hybrid: `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "declined-nullable-default"`;
- <a id="s2-17-p7"></a>[2.17¶7] on a ladder rung: `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_SEL "declined-nullable"`. On the size rung the artifact ships with no prefilter, which is smaller than a collapsed one, so the rung still rescues the compile.

<a id="s2-17-p8"></a>[2.17¶8] **The overrides.** `-fprefilter` outranks the decline: it is do-or-die and is never answered with its opposite. On an ordinary hybrid and on the size rung it keeps a prefilter (the exact one, or on the size rung the collapsed one, the only one that fits); on the DFA-overflow rung `-fprefilter` makes the rung ineligible, so the compile refuses. `-fprefilter-collapse` and `-fno-prefilter` do not override the decline: the first chooses a language for a filter, not whether one exists, and the second reaches the same artifact by its own door.

<a id="s2-17-p9"></a>[2.17¶9] **A rung is offered only where the collapse can help.** Both rungs are skipped when the retry would rebuild the machine that just failed: when the pattern has no collapsible repeat (the collapsed language is the exact one), and when the language is nullable but not `empty_admits` and `-fprefilter` is absent (the exact machine would be rebuilt). The ladder's next row then takes the same arrival, and a `size cap retry` figure in `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_WHY` is the exact artifact's.

<a id="s2-17-p10"></a>[2.17¶10] **What the two flags do.**

- <a id="s2-17-p11"></a>[2.17¶11] `-fprefilter-collapse` collapses wherever a collapsible repeat exists and the collapsed language is not declined, regardless of size or of any rung. It is the only route to count-independence: under it `((a)|b){0,400}c` and `((a)|b){0,4000}c` emit the same number of lines.
- <a id="s2-17-p12"></a>[2.17¶12] `-fno-prefilter-collapse` denies both rungs. On a pattern whose exact build succeeds the artifact is byte-identical to the default; on one that needed a rung the ladder's next row applies — the prefilter drop of §2.5 — so the pattern ships with no prefilter rather than a superset one. A caller who would rather be told the pattern is oversize passes `--size-cap=refuse` (`limits.md` §8.4).

<a id="s2-17-p13"></a>[2.17¶13] **Two conditions are correctness, and no flag reaches them.** The collapse never applies when the DFA is the ENGINE (a superset there would be a miscompile), and a pattern with no collapsible repeat is its own collapse: `-fprefilter-collapse` on it is honoured and vacuous (`_LANG_WHY "no counted repeat"`). The nullable decline is a cost rule, not a soundness one, and `-fprefilter` overrides it.

<a id="s2-17-p14"></a>[2.17¶14] **What the collapse costs.** The exact prefilter seeds the VM at the true leftmost start; the collapsed one seeds a lower bound the VM walks forward from, and because a superset's span end is not an upper bound a collapsed artifact carries `<PREFIX>_VM_PRUNE_CEILING "subject-end"` where the exact one carries `"prefilter-window"` (`ir_listing.md` §3.1.2). Both cost match time on some subjects, and the lost ceiling also costs step-budget headroom: `(a{1,3}){65}` on a long run of `a` answers with the exact prefilter and returns `PCREC_ERR_STEPS` with the collapsed one. The worst shape is a long run of the repeat's body followed by the terminator, where the exact reverse machine names the true start and the collapsed one names 0. On a subject the prefilter rejects outright, the smaller collapsed machine can be faster. The measurements are `docs/design/prefilter_count_independence.md` §7 and §10a.

<a id="s2-17-p15"></a>[2.17¶15] **The stamps.** `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG`, `"exact"` or `"count-collapsed"`, is emitted exactly where `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER` reads `"hybrid"`. It reports what was built and the count-collapse axis only: `"exact"` means the language was not count-collapsed, not that the prefilter recognises the pattern's own language (lookaround, atomic and `\K` hybrids read `"exact"` with an over-approximating prefilter); whether the prefilter proves the window end is `<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED "exact"` (§2.35). `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG_WHY` beside it says why:

| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"forced"` | `-fprefilter-collapse` collapsed a pattern that had something to collapse, with no rung involved |
| `"exact"` | the pattern's own language, the default outcome |
| `"no counted repeat"` | nothing to collapse: the collapsed language is the exact one (`-fprefilter-collapse` honoured but vacuous) |
| `"nullable collapsed language"` | documented and not emitted: a collapse introduces nullability only where the exact language is nullable too, and the decline above fires first |
| `"dfa overflow retry, exact nfa N"` | the DFA-overflow rung; `N` is the exact machine's size |
| `"size cap retry, exact N > cap"` | the size rung; `N` and `cap` are emitted bytes |

<a id="s2-17-p16"></a>[2.17¶16] There is no `"denied"` value: on a pattern whose exact build succeeds `-fno-prefilter-collapse` changes nothing, and on one that needed a rung it leaves no prefilter to stamp. `prefilter_lang_why` and `prefilter_collapsed` are written by one branch of `src/core/compile.c`'s build gate, so the two lines cannot disagree.

<a id="s2-17-p17"></a>[2.17¶17] **Dial:** no cell, GATE 4 (§5.4).

<a id="s2-18"></a>
### 2.18 `-fno-scan-edge` — `PCREC_NO_SCAN_EDGE` (bit 21)

<a id="s2-18-p1"></a>[2.18¶1] **Denies** SCAN EDGES: collapsing a DFA machine's counted class runs into bounded cursor loops. A run is a maximal sequence of states that differ only in how many bytes of one fixed class have been counted, every one leaving by the same door on every other byte and carrying the same accept bit: `[a-z]{0,16384}`'s forward machine is one run of 16,384 states plus the state that has counted them all, `[a-z]*` and `[a-z]+` are the one-state unbounded form, and `[0-9]{16}` is a run of sixteen. The pass is `src/opt/scanedge.c`, whose header states the criterion and its preconditions. Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only. Design: `docs/design/opt5_step2_twopass.md` and `docs/dev/opt5_step0_profile.md`.

<a id="s2-18-p2"></a>[2.18¶2] **What the artifact does instead.** One block per edge counts the class's bytes in a loop whose only carried value is the cursor, in place of the table walk whose load address is the previous load's result:

```c
if (forward_state == 0) {
    unsigned long scan_run_length = 0;
    while ((scan_position < subject_length) && scan_run_length < 16ULL && ((unsigned char)(subject[scan_position] - 48) <= 9)) {
        scan_position++;
        scan_run_length++;
    }
    if (scan_run_length == 16UL) { forward_state = 2; last_accept_position = scan_position; }
}
```

<a id="s2-18-p3"></a>[2.18¶3] The edge blocks sit off the loop's generic path. A machine's edge heads are numbered as its top rows, and the loop's one per-iteration state test is `<prefix>_<m>_is_stop`, which answers "dead or a head" in one unsigned compare; the edge blocks are reached only from that test, so the generic path carries no per-edge compare. The loop's entry asks the same question once per search, because the start seed can land the state on a head: `if (<m>_is_stop(state) && !<m>_is_dead(state)) goto <prefix>_forward_scan_edge;`, folded away on a machine with no seed.

```c
for (;;) {
    if (<m>_accepts(state)) last_accept_position = scan_position;
  <prefix>_forward_scan_views:
    if (scan_position >= subject_length) break;
    state = <m>_step(next_state, state, byte_class[subject[scan_position++]]);
    if (!<m>_is_stop(state)) continue;            /* the generic path */
    if (<m>_is_dead(state)) break;
    /* … the edge blocks … */
    goto <prefix>_forward_scan_views;
}
```

<a id="s2-18-p4"></a>[2.18¶4] **What a caller can see.** An edge-bearing machine's state numbers differ from the no-edge numbering (the heads are the top rows); each such machine emits `<prefix>_<m>_is_stop` (the constant `1` where every state is a head); the run's interior states are deleted, so the axis moves per-state table sizes as well as code; and an artifact with no scan edge — every artifact under this flag — has neither. No answer moves either way.

<a id="s2-18-p5"></a>[2.18¶5] **The preconditions a caller meets.** A run is collapsed only where every state of it has no position view and an accept bit that does not vary with the next byte's class (`\b`, `(?m)$`); §2.37 lifts part of the first condition. A chain head may not be a state any seed family names on a machine whose candidate-start prefilter writes the state variable (the `offset-set` pair, whose skip re-seeds). Two linked chains need their heads in ascending order. The shortest bounded run collapsed is `PCREC_MIN_SCAN_CHAIN` states and a machine carries at most `PCREC_MAX_SCAN_EDGES` edges, the longest runs first (`pcrec --list-limits`). An `attempt` scan (a `^`-anchored pattern) is not eligible: its states are code labels with no table load to shorten. Each of these is a decline, never a refusal: a declined run compiles as a table walk.

<a id="s2-18-p6"></a>[2.18¶6] **Two axes in `--list-axes`.**

| axis | candidates | question |
|---|---|---|
| `scan-edge` | `scan-edge`, `table-walk` | per state: does this state emit an edge? This flag removes the first candidate. |
| `scan-body` | `range`, `fold`, `kit`, `bitmap` | per edge: which run test does the edge use? Not this flag's: the class-form table's (below). |

<a id="s2-18-p7"></a>[2.18¶7] **The run test is the class-form table's answer.** A scan edge asks `src/gen/clskit.c`'s class-form table (§2.33, §5.4's λ row) for its class's form at the artifact's `--tune` position and at the SCAN site, and writes the answer through the emitters a VM class read uses. The byte rows give `range` (one interval, a compare against immediates), `fold` (an ASCII case pair, `(b | 0x20) == x`, at `−2`/`−1` only), `kit` (the class's kit matcher, at `−2`/`−1` only and only where it is smaller than the edge's table) or a table read — the table selection's `scan-table` row, one 256-byte table per edge. `-fno-cls-fold` denies the fold and `-fno-cls-kit` the kit, here as on the VM (§2.22, §2.33). At the default positions a fold pair on a scan edge is a table.

<a id="s2-18-p8"></a>[2.18¶8] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE` (§3): `"range"`, `"fold"`, `"kit"` or `"bitmap"` when every edge the artifact carries took that form, `"mixed"` when its edges took more than one, `"none"` when it carries none. A VM hybrid that inlines a DFA scan carries it too.

<a id="s2-18-p9"></a>[2.18¶9] **Reserved, not built.** A SIMD run-extension form of the edge's loop, per-ISA gated with the scalar loop as the fallback; and a period-`k` chain (a literal string's counted loop, `(?:ab){1,100}`), for which `DState.scan_period` carries the period — only period 1 is built, and a chain whose mid-period states disagree about their exit takes the table walk.

<a id="s2-18-p10"></a>[2.18¶10] **Dial:** no cell: flat (§5.4).

<a id="s2-19"></a>
### 2.19 `-fno-start-pinned` — `PCREC_NO_START_PINNED` (bit 22)

<a id="s2-19-p1"></a>[2.19¶1] **Denies** the PINNED START, axis `search-start` in `--list-axes`. A DFA search runs two scans: the forward one finds where a match ends, and a backwards one over an independently built REVERSE machine finds where that match began. When the forward machine's start state accepts unconditionally — at every position, under every position view and in every class context — a match exists wherever the search begins, accept pruning (D3) has removed the start-anywhere self-loop from every accepting closure, and every accept the forward loop records belongs to a thread that began at `search_from`. The backwards scan would then end at exactly `search_from`, so the pinned form returns it without one, and the reverse machine is not emitted at all (no tables, no accessors, no reverse loop):

```c
if (last_accept_position == (size_t)-1) return 0;
if (capture_spans) { capture_spans[0][0] = (ptrdiff_t)search_from;
                     capture_spans[0][1] = (ptrdiff_t)last_accept_position; }
return 1;
```

<a id="s2-19-p2"></a>[2.19¶2] `[a-z]{0,4096}`, `a*`, `.*` and `\w*` take it; `abc`, `[a-z]{4096,}` and `(?m)a*$` do not. Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only; a machine the predicate declines emits the reverse pass, a selection outcome and never a refusal. Design: `docs/design/opt5_step2_twopass.md`.

<a id="s2-19-p3"></a>[2.19¶3] **The `last_accept_position == (size_t)-1` gate is load-bearing.** A search at `startpos > 0` on a machine whose start state depends on a context byte can begin with no live closure; it records no accept, and "no match begins here" is the correct answer. The compiler also declines the pinned form on any machine with a dead seed state.

<a id="s2-19-p4"></a>[2.19¶4] **The denied build is a genuine control**: it recovers the start from an independently built automaton, where the default derives it from a proof about the forward machine, so `make test-axes`' sweep over this flag compares two derivations.

<a id="s2-19-p5"></a>[2.19¶5] **A VM hybrid is in scope**: it inlines the same search body as its prefilter, and consumes the span as a bound (`attempt_position = window[0][0]`), never as the answer.

<a id="s2-19-p6"></a>[2.19¶6] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_DFA_START`, `"pinned"` or `"reverse-pass"` (or `"attempt-start"` where the search recovers no start at all, `match_api.md` §6.3.4¶11), mirrored at run time by `rx_info.search_form` (§3, §3.2).

<a id="s2-19-p7"></a>[2.19¶7] **Dial:** no cell, PURE WIN (§5.4).

<a id="s2-20"></a>
### 2.20 `-fno-alt-island` — `PCREC_NO_ALT_ISLAND` (bit 23)

<a id="s2-20-p1"></a>[2.20¶1] **Denies** the ALTERNATION ISLAND, axis `alt-island` in `--list-axes`. Without it, `src/gen/emit_vm.c` lowers an N-way alternation as a chain: one resume frame per untried branch, each branch its own run of byte tests, so matching the last of N branches costs N − 1 push/fail/pop round trips. The island replaces that with a TRIE over the alternatives' literal bytes: a byte compare at a node with one child, a `switch` on the subject byte at a node with several, and one try site per node where an alternative ends. Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only. VM route only: the DFA determinizes the same trie on its own, so no DFA artifact carries the stamp.

<a id="s2-20-p2"></a>[2.20¶2] **What it applies to.** The island is built when the alternation's whole subtree matches a FINITE set of literal byte strings — every element a one-byte class, every combination enumerable within the island's budgets (`VM_ISL_MAX_WORDS`, `VM_ISL_MAX_BYTES`, `VM_ISL_MAX_DEPTH`). The predicate is over the language, not the branch list, so it does not depend on how far §2.7's factoring got. Each of these declines, and the alternation keeps the chain:

| declined | why |
|---|---|
| any element that is not a one-byte class | a trie edge is a byte; a multi-byte class edge would break the disjoint-siblings property the exactness argument rests on |
| a quantifier, a group, a capture, a backreference, a lookaround, an assertion, a subroutine call | the language is not a finite literal set, or the VM is needed inside the alternation |
| a caseless alternation | D23 folds a caseless letter to a two-member class at parse time |
| a literal set over the enumeration budgets | the cross product of concatenated alternations is exponential |
| fewer than `VM_ISL_MIN_BRANCHES` literal alternatives | there is no dispatch to make |
| fewer than `VM_ISL_MIN_BRANCHES_PREFIXED` alternatives, for an island that pushes | an island whose alternatives are not prefix-free keeps a resume frame, and below that width it is more work than the chain |
| an estimated emitted size above `VM_ISL_SIZE_FACTOR` times the chain's | bounded against the chain, so the axis never makes a pattern exceed a cap the chain fits |

<a id="s2-20-p3"></a>[2.20¶3] The width knees and the size factor are `selection knee` rows of `pcrec --list-limits`; they promise a caller nothing and have no `limits.md` section.

<a id="s2-20-p4"></a>[2.20¶4] **No answer moves, structurally.** Leftmost-first over an alternation of literals picks the least index of an alternative that matches here, never the longest (`abc|a|abd` on `abd` is the `a` branch). Every trie edge is one byte, so siblings are disjoint and a subject selects one root-to-leaf path; the alternatives that match are the ones ending on it, and when the continuation fails the island tries them in ascending original index, as the chain does. The set still live where the walk stops is a compile-time function of the node, so the island writes it as a chain of try sites and allocates no slot.

<a id="s2-20-p5"></a>[2.20¶5] **Identity is modulo which budget binds.** The island charges its trie walk to the WORK counter where the chain spends a STEP per branch resume, so where the chain's step budget binds and the island's does not, the island answers where the chain returns `PCREC_ERR_STEPS`. The island does strictly less stepping, so the direction is one-way: it can answer where the chain gives up, never the reverse.

<a id="s2-20-p6"></a>[2.20¶6] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_VM_ALT_ISLANDS`, a count. `tests/island/run_island_tests.sh` carries a cross-product ladder asserting that the refusal set is the chain's.

<a id="s2-20-p7"></a>[2.20¶7] **Dial:** no cell, PURE WIN (§5.4).

<a id="s2-21"></a>
### 2.21 `--vm-entry-shape=N` — the VM entry chain's shape

<a id="s2-21-p1"></a>[2.21¶1] Not a bit of `pcrec_options.flags`: the separate field `vm_entry_shape`. The CLI accepts an integer in `0..4`. A VM artifact's six entries (`<prefix>_search`, `_search_in`, `_match`, `_match_in`, `_match_caps`, `_match_caps_in`) sit on three `_run` helpers over one matcher body, `<prefix>_match_anchored`. The value chooses how many copies of the body the artifact carries and whether the un-suffixed entries bind storage or forward:

| N | token | shape |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | — | AUTO, the default: the size term below chooses |
| 1 | `plain` | no attribute. One body; six entries, each with its own frame, its stack-protector canary and an out-of-line call |
| 2 | `shared` | the body `noinline` (one copy, called); the three un-suffixed entries forward to their `_in` siblings through a static empty descriptor, with no frame and no canary |
| 3 | `forward` | the same forwards, body inlined: three copies, in the three `_in` entries, and no canary anywhere |
| 4 | `inline` | six copies |

<a id="s2-21-p2"></a>[2.21¶2] ANSWER-IDENTICAL across every value: the emitted matcher program is byte-identical across all five, and only the entry scaffolding above `goto <prefix>_L0;` moves. Not a flags bit, so it has no `rx_info.flags` question.

<a id="s2-21-p3"></a>[2.21¶3] **A value the artifact cannot honour is a selection outcome, never a refusal.** Values 2-4 need a frameless artifact (`<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS 1`): gcc refuses `always_inline` on a function containing a computed goto, and on a framed artifact the storage is live, so a framed artifact takes `plain`. Values 2 and 3 also need an artifact that never writes the working storage — no `RX_PUSH`, no linked call and no `RX_SET` — because the forward binds an empty descriptor; the trail is real storage even on a frameless artifact. Where a forward rung is illegal the fallback keeps the body count's family: `shared` falls to `plain` and `forward` to `inline`.

<a id="s2-21-p4"></a>[2.21¶4] **AUTO.** `VM_INLINE_CHAIN_MAX_BYTES` (4,096 at `--tune=0`; §5.4 moves it) is compared with the artifact's program bytes, stamped as `<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES` — measured at the canonical two-byte prefix, so `-p` never moves the rung (`limits.md` §8.2), and excluding SIMD-guarded bytes, so `-fmemfn-simd` never moves it (`limits.md` §8.3). At or below the term AUTO takes `forward`, above it `shared`; where the forward rungs are illegal, `inline` below the term and `plain` above it. `forward` measures within noise of `inline`, and `shared` at `plain`'s run time; a caller who wants the forwarding win on a large artifact asks for `--vm-entry-shape=3`. Measurement: `docs/dev/lanes/ccd2_report.md`.

<a id="s2-21-p5"></a>[2.21¶5] **The stamps** are `<PREFIX>_VM_ENTRY_SHAPE` (the token) and `<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES` (the number the term compared), on every VM artifact including a hybrid and on no pure-DFA artifact (`match_api.md` §6.3). Two stamps, because `plain` has four causes (framed, forward-illegal and large, asked for, or a tiered artifact) and the token alone does not say which.

<a id="s2-21-p6"></a>[2.21¶6] **What `make test-axes` sweeps.** Every run sweeps `forward` (what AUTO takes below the term) and `inline` (the max-speed end); all four values only under `AXES_FULL=1`, which the merge battery's axes stage exports (`scripts/battery.sh`). `tests/axes/run_axes.sh` prints its tier in its summary, so a two-value run is never quoted as a four-value one.

<a id="s2-21-p7"></a>[2.21¶7] **Dial:** the term, never a value of `N`: `4,096` at `0`, `8,192` at `+1` and `+2` (§5.4). An explicit `--vm-entry-shape=N` overrides whatever the dial set.

<a id="s2-22"></a>
### 2.22 `-fno-cls-fold` — `PCREC_NO_CLS_FOLD` (bit 24)

<a id="s2-22-p1"></a>[2.22¶1] **Denies** the FOLD COMPARE for an ASCII case pair, axis `cls-fold` in `--list-axes`. D23 folds a caseless letter into a two-member class at parse time (`(?i)a` is `{'A','a'}`). An ASCII fold pair — two letters differing only in bit `0x20` — is tested as `(byte | 0x20) == lower`, one or-mask and one compare, and its class table is not emitted. The rows are the class-form table's `byte-fold` (at `−2`/`−1`, both sites) and `byte-fold-default` (at `0`/`+1`/`+2`, the VM site only), both denied by this flag (`src/gen/clskit.c`, predicate `is_ascii_fold_pair`). Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only.

<a id="s2-22-p2"></a>[2.22¶2] **Where it reaches.** A VM program's class reads at every position, and a DFA scan edge's run test at `−2`/`−1`. At the default positions a scan edge's fold pair keeps its 256-byte table, so no DFA artifact moves under the flag there. The DFA's byte-class partition never reads the class-form table. Denied, the class falls to the next byte row: its table at `0`/`+1`/`+2`, and at `−2`/`−1` its kit matcher where that is smaller (§2.33).

<a id="s2-22-p3"></a>[2.22¶3] **Answer identity is structural**: `(b | 0x20) == (lo | 0x20)` holds for exactly the two bytes `{lo, lo | 0x20}`. gcc compiles the two-member test and the fold to the same branchless code with no load (`docs/dev/form_char_step0.md` §2; `studies/form_char_twins/`).

| declined | why |
|---|---|
| a set that is not exactly two members | the fold identity is about a pair |
| a pair not differing only in bit `0x20` (`[ac]`) | the or-mask would admit bytes outside the set |
| a `0x20` pair of non-letters (`` [@`] ``) | not what caseless folding produces; a wider two-member compare is not built |
| a scan edge's fold pair at `0`/`+1`/`+2` | the default positions keep the scan edge's table |

<a id="s2-22-p4"></a>[2.22¶4] **The stamps** are `<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_FOLDS`, a count, on a VM program, and `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "fold"` on a scan edge.

<a id="s2-22-p5"></a>[2.22¶5] **Dial:** no cell, NOT A RUNG: the fold is absorbed into the class-matcher kit, λ's row of §5.4.

<a id="s2-23"></a>
### 2.23 `-fno-startpos-guard` / `-fstartpos-guard=align` — `PCREC_NO_STARTPOS_GUARD` (bit 25) / `PCREC_FORCE_STARTPOS_ALIGN` (bit 40)

<a id="s2-23-p1"></a>[2.23¶1] A CONTRACT axis: the builds give different answers on one input class on purpose. It selects between three ruled semantics for a caller-supplied start position inside a character, and every value compiles to the same automaton and selects the same engine.

| | |
|---|---|
| **What it controls** | what the emitted entries do with a caller `startpos` (or `ctx->pos`) inside a character (`match_api.md` §9.2) |
| **Default** | refuse: the guard is on |
| **Values** | refuse (default); honour (`-fno-startpos-guard`); align forward (`-fstartpos-guard=align`). Passing both non-default spellings is refused |
| **Stamp** | `<PREFIX>_STARTPOS_GUARD`: `"guarded"`, `"permissive"` or `"align"` |
| **`rx_info.flags`** | kept, except under `byte` |
| **Inert under** | the `byte` encoding, where every position is a character boundary: the three builds are byte-identical and both bits are masked |

<a id="s2-23-p2"></a>[2.23¶2] **What the three values answer**, under an encoding with multi-byte characters:

- <a id="s2-23-p3"></a>[2.23¶3] **guarded** (default): a `startpos` inside a character is refused with `PCREC_ERR_STARTPOS` (`match_api.md` §4), libpcre2's `PCRE2_ERROR_BADUTFOFFSET` behaviour under `PCRE2_UTF`.
- <a id="s2-23-p4"></a>[2.23¶4] **permissive** (`-fno-startpos-guard`): the artifact answers at the position named, with the automaton's own answer. On a leading negative assertion that differs from both PCRE2 UTF modes in the succeeding direction: `(?<!.)` at offset 1 of `CE B1 CE B2` reports `(1,1)`.
- <a id="s2-23-p5"></a>[2.23¶5] **align** (`-fstartpos-guard=align`): a `startpos > 0` inside a character moves forward over continuation bytes to the next character start (or `n`), once, at entry, and a search runs as if that position had been passed; an anchored match-here entry answers `-1`. It is for a misaligned pointer into valid text, not a way to accept invalid UTF-8: under `-futf-check` (§2.36) the check runs from the aligned position. Each skipped position is a continuation byte, so no match a character start could report is lost.

<a id="s2-23-p6"></a>[2.23¶6] Only align rounds a caller's `startpos`, and only because it is asked for by name (`match_api.md` §9.2¶9). Offset 0 is not this axis's: it is never refused, and a subject that begins with continuation bytes is searched from its first non-continuation byte under every value (`match_api.md` §9.3).

<a id="s2-23-p7"></a>[2.23¶7] **What it does not touch.** The positions the ENGINE generates — an unanchored search's candidate starts, a failed attempt's retry, a search's first attempt — are character boundaries under every value, with no flag (K49, K50, K73). The guarantee is about what is reported: no match is ever reported starting at a non-boundary. Where the pattern cannot match empty the compiler omits the engine's boundary gate, because the pattern's own first-byte test already refuses every mid-character start; `src/ir/nfa.c`'s `cstart_check_omission` checks that at the omission site.

<a id="s2-23-p8"></a>[2.23¶8] **Differential:** `tests/utf8/run_startbnd_diff.sh` compiles one witness family both ways into one translation unit and sweeps every `startpos` of every subject: the builds must agree at every character boundary and diverge at exactly the mid-character set with the typed code, and an empty divergence population fails. A third arm asserts that a `byte` artifact is guard-free under either flag. `tests/utfcheck/`'s align arm compares an aligned call with libpcre2 at the aligned position.

<a id="s2-23-p9"></a>[2.23¶9] **`make test-axes` sweeps both non-default spellings for identity**, and the sweep is clean because the corpus cannot reach the divergence: only `tests/utf8/` compiles under `utf8`, and every corpus cell starts at offset 0 or a character boundary. The differential is the instrument that can see the axis.

<a id="s2-23-p10"></a>[2.23¶10] **Dial:** no cell, GATE 1 (§5.4).

<a id="s2-24"></a>
### 2.24 `-fno-comments` / `-fcomments` — `PCREC_NO_COMMENTS` (bit 26), `PCREC_FORCE_COMMENTS` (bit 27)

<a id="s2-24-p1"></a>[2.24¶1] **Controls** whether the emitted artifact carries its human commentary — the orientation block, the table legends, the per-label role text, the paragraph above each entry point. `--list-axes` reports it as `comments`, rows `essential-only` and `full`. A RENDERING axis, not an optimization: the code, the tables, the stamps, the object file and the answers are identical under both settings, because the C compiler discards comments.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Default** | off: a default artifact carries only its ESSENTIAL comments (D112) |
| **Stamp** | none |
| **`rx_info.flags`** | both bits masked |
| **Inert under** | nothing |

<a id="s2-24-p2"></a>[2.24¶2] Pass `-fcomments` to read the artifact.

<a id="s2-24-p3"></a>[2.24¶3] **The two classes** (D112), decided at the emission site, not by a filter over finished text:

- <a id="s2-24-p4"></a>[2.24¶4] **ESSENTIAL**, emitted under every setting: the generated-by line naming pcrec and the `abi` and echoing the pattern (`/* Generated by pcrec (abi N). Pattern: ... */`, on the `.c` and the `.h`), and the whole shared `PCREC_RX_ABI_H` type block — the `rx_ctx` fields, the `rx_matchfn` return space, the error codes and the `rx_info` fields (`match_api.md` §2). The feature-set line is not essential: its two values ship as the `PCREC_FEATURE_SET` and `PCREC_FEATURE_MODULES` `#define`s, which live only in the `.c`, so a default `.h` does not record the feature set.
- <a id="s2-24-p5"></a>[2.24¶5] **NON-ESSENTIAL**: everything else. This is what the axis removes.

<a id="s2-24-p6"></a>[2.24¶6] **It cannot rescue or refuse a pattern.** `PCREC_MAX_EMIT_BYTES` and `PCREC_MAX_EMIT_CODE_BYTES` are measured over the comment-excluded artifact (`limits.md` §8.1), so the refusal set is the same under both settings. The gain is source size and readability for an embedder shipping generated C, not object size or speed.

<a id="s2-24-p7"></a>[2.24¶7] **A force pair whose force restores.** A `config` block or a `--source` target can set either spelling, and the command line overrides it in both directions (`cli.md` §1.1). Passing both, the deny wins. There is no stamp: the comments' presence is their own record, and a stamp would still claim `"full"` on an artifact a tool had stripped.

<a id="s2-24-p8"></a>[2.24¶8] **Where the gate is.** One render-time decision in the emission kit (`pcrec_sb_cmt_open` / `pcrec_sb_cmt_close`, `src/core/sb.c`; D108): the emitters emit every comment event, and the buffer decides whether the text is written, so no comment is ever half-removed.

<a id="s2-25"></a>
### 2.25 `-fno-vm-anchor-bound` — `PCREC_NO_VM_ANCHOR_BOUND` (bit 28)

<a id="s2-25-p1"></a>[2.25¶1] **Denies** the VM's attempt-loop START BOUND. A pattern whose every alternative begins with `^` (outside multiline) or `\A` can match only at absolute offset 0; one whose every alternative begins with `\G` can match only at `search_from`. Either way at most one start can match, and with the axis on a VM artifact's attempt loop stops after it (`const size_t attempt_max = search_from;`, read by the loop's existing continue test in place of `subject_length`). Every other VM artifact and every DFA artifact is byte-identical under the flag. Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL: every attempt the bound removes is one that would have run and failed. Masked out of `rx_info.flags`.

<a id="s2-25-p2"></a>[2.25¶2] **Where the fact comes from.** One predicate, `pcrec_start_anchor` (`src/facts/startanch.c`), over the lowered AST above either engine. The DFA route keeps its own tighter derivation for its own loop and asserts that this one does not disagree in the unsound direction.

<a id="s2-25-p3"></a>[2.25¶3] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_VM_START` on every VM artifact: `"anchored"`, `"gstart"` or `"unanchored"`. A denied build reads `"unanchored"`, the same as a pattern with nothing to prove. It is the VM's reading of the fact `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN "attempt"` carries on the other engine.

<a id="s2-25-p4"></a>[2.25¶4] **Facts emptied** (`--emit-facts`, `docs/spec/facts_listing.md`): `start_anchor`.
A fact deny: the start-anchor fact reads `unanchored` for every consumer at once — the VM's attempt-loop bound and `<PREFIX>_VM_START`, the DFA route's agreement assertion, the pre-check admission's VM one-attempt arm (§2.29: a denied anchor never admits `"one-attempt"` on a VM route), and the hybrid re-seed table's `anchored` row (§2.35).

<a id="s2-26"></a>
### 2.26 `-fno-end-window` — `PCREC_NO_END_WINDOW` (bit 29)

<a id="s2-26-p1"></a>[2.26¶1] **Denies** the END-ANCHOR START WINDOW. When every alternative of a pattern ends in `$`, `\Z` or `\z` outside multiline, every match ends at the subject's end (or one byte before it, under `$`/`\Z`'s final-newline allowance). If the pattern's maximum width is also finite, every match begins within `maxw + eps` bytes of the end, and a search starts its scan there instead of at `search_from`. Both engines emit the clamp from the same fact through one emitter. Default: on. Masked out of `rx_info.flags`.

<a id="s2-26-p2"></a>[2.26¶2] **Where the fact comes from.** `pcrec_end_window` (`src/facts/endwin.c`), one walk over the lowered AST. It answers "no window" — never a guess — when the maximum width is unbounded; when the encoding has positions that are not character boundaries (a computed offset could land inside a character); when the pattern contains `\G` anywhere (its truth depends on the `search_from` the clamp moves); and on a multiline `$`.

<a id="s2-26-p3"></a>[2.26¶3] **ANSWER-IDENTICAL**, with a different risk from its neighbours: it moves the position a search starts at rather than removing work that would fail, so a window one byte too narrow would drop a legal `$`-before-final-newline match. `tests/assertions/end_window.rxt` carries each claim at a subject length that leaves the mechanism inert and at one that makes it fire.

<a id="s2-26-p4"></a>[2.26¶4] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW` on every artifact of both engines: the bound as a decimal string, or `"none"`. A string with a `"none"` member, because `0` is a legal window (a `\z` pattern of maximum width 0 may begin only at the end). A denied build reads `"none"`.

<a id="s2-26-p5"></a>[2.26¶5] **Facts emptied** (`--emit-facts`, `docs/spec/facts_listing.md`): `end_window`.
A fact deny: the end-window fact reads `none` for every consumer of it — both engines' start clamp and `<PREFIX>_END_WINDOW`.

<a id="s2-27"></a>
### 2.27 `-fno-req-byte` — `PCREC_NO_REQ_BYTE` (bit 30)

<a id="s2-27-p1"></a>[2.27¶1] **Denies** the NECESSARY-BYTE family. Where every match of a pattern must contain some literal byte, a search over a window that lacks it answers no-match in one `memchr`-class pass instead of an attempt at every start (PCRE2 records the same kind of fact as `PCRE2_INFO_LASTCODEUNIT`). This axis empties the whole family: the necessary set, the one-byte pick, the necessary run (§2.28) and everything that reads them. Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL: the check answers no-match only where every attempt would have failed. Masked out of `rx_info.flags`. It serves the VM route too, where the hybrid prefilter is declined for a backreference or a linked call.

<a id="s2-27-p2"></a>[2.27¶2] **How the set is derived.** A bottom-up walk of the lowered AST (`src/facts/req.c`): a concatenation unions, an alternation intersects, a quantifier admitting zero iterations contributes nothing, a one-byte class is a singleton, and a backreference, a linked call or any assertion contributes the empty set (which disables the check). A lookaround's body is not descended into: a lookbehind's bytes can lie before the window. Unlike PCRE2's per-attempt fact, the whole window counts: the check runs once per call over `[search_from, subject_length)`, where every byte of every match lies.

<a id="s2-27-p3"></a>[2.27¶3] **Which member is tested.** The member with the lowest byte-rate under the compile's declared analysis (`findings.md`), ties to the RIGHTMOST — the PICK kind's NONE answer (`findings.md` §4), which is also the answer where no byte-rate applies. The default analysis declares a byte-rate only under the `byte` encoding (`findings.md` §2), so under every other encoding the pick is the rightmost member. Every member is a byte every match contains, so the choice moves a speed and never an answer.

<a id="s2-27-p4"></a>[2.27¶4] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE` on every artifact of both engines: the byte as a decimal string, or `"none"` (a string with a `"none"` member, because `0` is a legal byte). Where §2.28's run shipped and its scan member is one exact byte, the stamp is that member, because there is one emitted `memchr` and the stamp reports what it tests. Where the run's scan member is a two-member cube (§2.39), the stamp is the set's pick, or `"none"` where the set is empty (`(?i)union.*?select.*?from`), so every value it carries is a member of the necessary set. The stamp names the ANALYSIS, not the emission: whether anything is emitted is `<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY` (§2.29).

<a id="s2-27-p5"></a>[2.27¶5] **Facts emptied** (`--emit-facts`, `docs/spec/facts_listing.md`): `req_set`, `req_whole_run`, `req_run`, `req_byte`.
A fact deny over the whole necessary-byte family: every consumer sees a pattern with nothing necessary — the one-byte and run pre-checks and their stamps, the no-DFA-scan route's whole-set and whole-run compares, the admission (`<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY "none"`), the dominance test, and the run PIN §2.30's run-pinned prefilter rows read, so this flag removes those rows' pin too (`docs/design/litscan_s1.md` §1.1).

<a id="s2-28"></a>
### 2.28 `-fno-req-run` — `PCREC_NO_REQ_RUN` (bit 31)

<a id="s2-28-p1"></a>[2.28¶1] **Denies** the NECESSARY RUN: §2.27's fact at word grain, the longest run of contiguous literal POSITIONS every match must contain. Where a run ships, the search scans for the run's rarest member and compares the whole run at each hit, so a window that holds the byte but not the run answers no-match in one pass. §2.27's one-byte check is this mechanism's length-1 case. Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL: the run is necessary. Masked out of `rx_info.flags`.

<a id="s2-28-p2"></a>[2.28¶2] **Relation to `-fno-req-byte`.** Denying `-fno-req-byte` denies this too: there is no run check without a byte to scan for. Denying `-fno-req-run` alone leaves the one-byte check standing, byte-identical to its output without this axis.

<a id="s2-28-p3"></a>[2.28¶3] **How the run is derived.** The same walk as §2.27, with a second accumulator (`src/facts/req.c`): a concatenation joins the left factor's guaranteed literal suffix to the right factor's guaranteed literal prefix; an alternation keeps its branches' longest common prefix and suffix; nothing is joined across a repeat's iterations (`(?:ab){2,}` reports `ab`); a quantifier admitting zero iterations breaks contiguity (the opposite would delete a match where the repeat takes none); and everything that breaks the byte analysis breaks the run. Each of these is a missed opportunity, never an unsound claim.

<a id="s2-28-p4"></a>[2.28¶4] **A run is a run of POSITIONS.** A position is one byte or one two-member CUBE `(T, K)` — the bytes `x` with `(x & K) == T`, `K` `0xff` for a byte and one clear bit for a pair, `T` the lower member (§2.39). A class that is neither breaks contiguity. A run's information is the sum over its positions of `popcount(K)` (8 per byte, 7 per pair); among exact runs that ranks by length. A run ships only where its information is at least `PCREC_MIN_REQ_RUN_BITS` — every exact run of two bytes or more, and three caseless letters but not two. An alternation's common prefix and suffix are, position by position, the smallest cube holding both branches' positions (`K' = Ka & Kb & ~(Ta ^ Tb)`, `T' = Ta & K'`), stopping at the first position whose hull has more than two members: `frank|fred` reports `fr[ae]`.

<a id="s2-28-p5"></a>[2.28¶5] **Which member is scanned, and truncation.** The member with the lowest byte-rate (a pair counts both its members), ties to the RIGHTMOST — the PICK kind's NONE answer (`findings.md` §4), which is also the answer where no byte-rate applies. The rightmost rule keeps a scan off UTF-8 lead bytes, which a run opening mid-character would otherwise pick. A run longer than `PCREC_MAX_REQ_RUN_EMIT` positions is truncated, never split into two compares: to the window of that length containing the scan member whose members sum to the lowest byte-rate mass, ties leftmost, and so, where no byte-rate applies, to the leftmost admissible window. 8 is where gcc lowers a constant-length `memcmp` to one word load and one compare. A masked run is compared masked by the run compare's `words`/`bytes` rows (§2.38), and a pair scan member is scanned as two `memchr` streams, one per member, inside the block's one guarded loop.
