<a id="s2-28-p6"></a>[2.28¶6] **No decline rule.** One constant-length compare per occurrence of the scanned member costs something where the run is as common as its rarest byte, and the axis ships with no rule to predict that: a run's rate is a joint property the byte-rate cannot predict (`docs/design/reqpos_2b.md` §4.2). This flag is the decline.

<a id="s2-28-p7"></a>[2.28¶7] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN` on every artifact of both engines: the run's bytes as lowercase hex, `@`, the scanned member's index — `2e746172@0` for `.tar` — then, only where some position is not an exact byte, `/` and each position's `K` in hex — `53454c454354@4/dfdfdfdfdfdf` for `(?i)select` — or `"none"`. `<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE` is exactly `bytes[idx]` wherever `mask[idx]` is `ff`, so the two stamps are checkable against each other. It names the analysis, not the emission (§2.29).

<a id="s2-28-p8"></a>[2.28¶8] **Facts emptied** (`--emit-facts`, `docs/spec/facts_listing.md`): `req_whole_run`, `req_run`.
A fact deny over the run: every consumer sees no run — the run pre-check and `<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN`, the no-DFA-scan route's whole-run compare, the dominance test's run conjuncts, and the run pin §2.30's rows read. The necessary set and the one-byte pick are untouched.

<a id="s2-29"></a>
### 2.29 The pre-checks' ADMISSION — `<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY`, the `req-admit` table

<a id="s2-29-p1"></a>[2.29¶1] Not an axis with a flag of its own: the rule that decides whether §2.27's and §2.28's pre-check is emitted at all, and in which shape. It is stated here because its outcome is caller-observable — one stamp, and the presence of a `memchr` in the artifact. It is a first-match table of five rows, listed by `--list-axes` as axis `req-admit` (the presence rows of the start table `cand_rows[]`), in this order: `none`, `one-attempt`, `dominated`, `set-leads`, `emitted`. The first row whose predicate holds decides. Only `set-leads` has a deny bit (`-fno-req-set-lead`, §2.40). A second table, `req-use` (§2.41), decides what the body does with an emitted run pre-check's answer and calls this one.

<a id="s2-29-p2"></a>[2.29¶2] **`one-attempt`: not in front of an exit that is already cheaper.** Where the artifact's search route tries exactly one start position, linearly, a whole-window pass only adds work. On the DFA side the route is one attempt when every interior start state is dead (`^`-anchored, or `\G`-anchored); on the VM side when `<PREFIX>_VM_START` is `"anchored"` or `"gstart"` AND the attempt is linear by a fact the artifact states: an exact-language hybrid DFA runs in front (`<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "hybrid"` with `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER_LANG "exact"`), or the program is frameless (`<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS 1`). A framed one-attempt VM program with no prefilter or a collapsed one can backtrack exponentially before failing — `^([a-zA-Z0-9._%+-]+)+@` under `--engine=vm` on a long class run with no `@` returns `PCREC_ERR_STEPS` without the check — so there the pre-check is a no-match proof that bounds the call, and it is emitted.

<a id="s2-29-p3"></a>[2.29¶3] **On a VM route with no DFA scan, an emitted pre-check tests the WHOLE necessary set.** Where `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER` is `"none"` the pre-check is the call's only linear no-match proof, so the emitted check (§2.27's byte or §2.28's run) is followed by one `memchr` per remaining member of the necessary set, and any absent member answers no-match. Whether the call is proved a no-match then depends on the set, a fact about the pattern, and not on which member the pick chose. An artifact whose set is its pick alone (or its run's bytes alone) emits nothing more. Where a DFA scan runs in front, nothing changes.

<a id="s2-29-p4"></a>[2.29¶4] **On the same route, a run longer than its window is compared WHOLE.** §2.28 truncates a long run to one window, and `<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN` names that window. On a VM artifact with `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none"` the window's compare is followed by one compare of the whole run as the analysis holds it (up to `PCREC_MAX_REQ_RUN_SCAN` bytes), scanned on the same member, and its absence answers no-match. A masked run is compared masked in both blocks. The whole-set half above then skips every EXACT position's byte of the whole run; a pair position proves only that one of its members is present, so a set member equal to its `T` keeps its own `memchr`.

<a id="s2-29-p5"></a>[2.29¶5] **`dominated`: not a second pass on a byte already scanned.** Let `p` be the byte the artifact's own candidate-start scan runs on: the `memchr` form's byte, or the scan byte of an `offset-set` or `run-pinned` prefilter. A `byte-class` prefilter scans no single byte, and an artifact with no DFA scan has no `p`. The pre-check on `q` is declined where:

- <a id="s2-29-p6"></a>[2.29¶6] **identity**: `p == q`, under every encoding. For a run pre-check identity is required AND the scan's candidate test must itself refuse every window lacking the run — test every position of the run at the offset where it is pinned from every match's start (an `offset-set` selection whose verifies cover the run, or a `run-pinned` prefilter). Over a masked run a pair position must be tested by a byte or a term whose members all lie in its cube: `(?i)x/1234`'s offset-0 term `{x, X}` verifies it, while `a[bc]de`, whose prefilter tests nothing at offset 1, keeps its pre-check;
- <a id="s2-29-p7"></a>[2.29¶7] **density**, for the one-byte pre-check under a `memchr`-form prefilter only: `q` is not strictly rarer than `p` by the byte-rate — the COMPARE kind's question, whose NONE answer is "no density claim", so where no byte-rate applies only identity declines.

<a id="s2-29-p8"></a>[2.29¶8] **`set-leads`**: §2.40.

<a id="s2-29-p9"></a>[2.29¶9] **Answer identity, including give-ups.** A declined pre-check is a check not run, and the check could only return no-match where the engine below it then returns no-match within the same budget — which the linearity condition of `one-attempt` guarantees. The whole-set and whole-run compares on the no-DFA-scan route are what make that route's answer rest on the pattern rather than on the pick.

<a id="s2-29-p10"></a>[2.29¶10] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY` on every artifact of both engines, a closed four-token set answering WHETHER a pre-check is emitted (`set-leads` is a shape of an emitted one):

| value | meaning |
|---|---|
| `"emitted"` | the artifact emits a pre-check, on the byte or run its siblings name (under `set-leads`, on a rarer necessary-set byte first) |
| `"none"` | nothing is necessary: no necessary byte and no necessary run |
| `"one-attempt"` | declined: the route tries one start position, linearly |
| `"dominated"` | declined: an equally rare byte is already scanned (for a run, by a candidate test that also verifies the run) |

<a id="s2-29-p11"></a>[2.29¶11] `"none"` holds if and only if `<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE` and `<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN` are both `"none"`. A masked run over an empty necessary set has `<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE "none"` and an emitted pre-check. A declined artifact whose body calls no other `memchr` has no `#include <string.h>`.

<a id="s2-30"></a>
### 2.30 `-fno-run-prefilter` — `PCREC_NO_RUN_PREFILTER` (bit 32)

<a id="s2-30-p1"></a>[2.30¶1] **Denies** the RUN-PINNED prefilter rows. Where the pattern's necessary run (§2.28, `<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN`) sits at a fixed offset from every match's start — §2.14's offset walk proves each of its positions there — and the forward DFA scan already scans the run's scan member at that offset (the offset-0 `memchr` byte, or the offset-set selection's scan offset), the prefilter verifies the whole run on each candidate as one constant-length compare inside its offset-skip block, and the run pre-check is then dominated (§2.29) and not emitted. The run is verified as one term, outside §2.14's set cap. Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only. Design: `docs/design/litscan_s1.md`.

<a id="s2-30-p2"></a>[2.30¶2] **The stamps.** `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER` reads `"run-pinned"` or, under a view or word context, `"run-pinned-bounded"`; `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS` lists every offset the test covers, and its scan may be offset 0 (`"0*,1,2,3,4"` on `/user|/users`), which no other value's is.

<a id="s2-30-p3"></a>[2.30¶3] **The deny is two bits.** The rows carry `PCREC_NO_RUN_PREFILTER | PCREC_NO_OFFSET_SKIP`: they emit §2.14's block, so `-fno-offset-skip` removes them too. `--list-axes` renders the pair `|`-joined (`registry.md` §6). With this flag alone the prefilter falls back to `memchr[-bounded]` or `offset-set[-bounded]` and the run pre-check returns (`<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY "emitted"`). Declining a pre-check an `offset-set` selection already dominates is admission (§2.29), not this axis. `-fno-req-run` and `-fno-req-byte` remove the run itself, so nothing is pinned under either.

<a id="s2-30-p4"></a>[2.30¶4] **The pin is a fact about EXACT positions.** On a masked run (§2.39) it pins the maximal stretch of exact positions around the window's rarest exact byte (`--emit-facts`' `run_pin` reads `o:at+len` for such a stretch and `o` for a whole-window pin), and the rows' term and scan are that stretch's, compared exactly: no masked run enters `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER`'s rows. `-fno-req-run-fold` narrows the run, and the pin reads the narrowed run.

<a id="s2-31"></a>
### 2.31 `-fno-lit-run` — `PCREC_NO_LIT_RUN` (bit 33)

<a id="s2-31-p1"></a>[2.31¶1] **Denies** the VM's LITERAL-RUN compare. In a concatenation, three or more consecutive elements that are each one exact byte form a run, consumed by one bounds check and one constant-length compare under one label, in place of a per-byte chain: `if (scan_position + L <= subject_length && !memcmp(subject + scan_position, "<run>", L))`. In an alternation island (§2.20) a trie node's single-child chain, down to the first node that branches or where an alternative ends, is the same compare. The compare is the literal-compare kit's one emitter — the run compare of §2.38, shared with the run-pinned rows (§2.30) and the run pre-check — so at the lengths §2.38's `overlap` row takes it is two overlapping word compares. Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only; the deny is the literal-compare kit's row flag (D122 addendum 2).

<a id="s2-31-p2"></a>[2.31¶2] **The floor is three bytes.** A two-byte run stays a byte chain: the floor is part of `pcrec_lit_run`'s own predicate (`src/core/cpset.c`), the one node-grain fact the chain emission, the cost walk and the slot walk share. It is not a flag. The island's single-child chain has its own commit rule.

<a id="s2-31-p3"></a>[2.31¶3] **What ends a run.** Any element that is not one exact byte: a class of two or more bytes (every letter under `(?i)`), a capture's open or close, a repeat, an atomic group, a lookaround, an assertion. A capture or a choice point between two bytes is program the matcher executes there, which is why this run is not §2.28's necessary run (contiguous in the subject, across captures). The backward walk (lookbehind bodies, the reverse-deterministic rung) and the cursor rung's fixed-length body keep per-byte compares.

<a id="s2-31-p4"></a>[2.31¶4] **No answer and no give-up moves.** The compare accepts exactly the bytes the chain accepted, reads exactly `L` bytes after one `pos + L <= n` test, and the step, work and node budgets charge what the chain charged (`limits.md` §3.1). `<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES` and the label count move with the program text; the island size rule's estimates (§2.20) do not. An artifact gains `#include <string.h>` if nothing else in it needed one.

<a id="s2-31-p5"></a>[2.31¶5] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_VM_LIT_RUNS`, the number of run compares the program writes; `0` on every VM artifact that writes none and under the flag. Denied, the program is the per-byte chain, byte for byte apart from that stamp line.

<a id="s2-32"></a>
### 2.32 `-fno-ctx-node` — `PCREC_NO_CTX_NODE` (bit 35)

<a id="s2-32-p1"></a>[2.32¶1] **Denies** the CONTEXT NODE for a one-character lookaround, axis `ctx-node`. The lowering is a first-match table of two rows, read live off `src/parse/ctxnode.c`'s `pcrec_look_rows` by `--list-axes` (design `docs/design/ucp_design.md` §0.1, §2.2):

| # | row | deny | applies | action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ctx-node` | `-fno-ctx-node` | the body is capture-free and assertion-free, its language is a set of single characters, and every member is one byte of the encoding | the context node: `(?<=C)`, `(?<!C)`, `(?=C)`, `(?!C)` (and the non-atomic and alpha spellings) read "is the previous / next character in `C`" |
| 2 | `lookaround` | — | always | the lookaround's VM sub-match |

<a id="s2-32-p2"></a>[2.32¶2] The predicate is over the language, not the spelling: `(?<=a|b)` and `(?<=[ab])` are the same node, and `(?=a?)`, `(?<=ab)`, `(?<=(a))` are not. The context node is what `\b`/`\B` are: the DFA carries it on its class axis (a per-machine list of context sets, whose atoms index every per-state view) and the VM tests it as one guarded byte read. `\b` and `\B` build the node directly and are not affected by the flag. Under `-e utf8` every member must be ASCII: a non-ASCII member is not readable byte-wise (`(?<=[^a])a` on `80 61` would read the stray continuation byte as in `[^a]`), so such a set takes row 2. Default: on.

<a id="s2-32-p3"></a>[2.32¶3] ANSWER-IDENTICAL, and ENGINE-MOVING without being kept in `rx_info.flags`. A pattern whose only DFA-excluding construct is such a lookaround compiles to the DFA with the node and to the VM under the denial; `--engine=dfa` with the denial refuses (`(?<=...) requires the VM engine, which --engine=dfa excludes`, on `(?<=a)b` with `--features lookaround`). The bit is masked: an artifact built under the flag reports the same `.flags` as one built without it, and `<PREFIX>_ENGINE` (`"vm"` under the denial, `"dfa"` without) is the observable consequence. No stamp of its own.

<a id="s2-32-p4"></a>[2.32¶4] A DFA machine carries at most `PCREC_MAX_CTX_SETS` distinct context sets and `PCREC_MAX_CTX_ATOMS` atoms (`limits.md` §3.9); over either, the DFA is declined as for a state-cap overflow (§2.11). `tests/ucp/run_ctxnode_tests.sh` runs the context-node corpus both ways.

<a id="s2-33"></a>
### 2.33 `-fno-cls-kit` — `PCREC_NO_CLS_KIT` (bit 36)

<a id="s2-33-p1"></a>[2.33¶1] **Denies** the CLASS-MATCHER KIT, the one kit-level deny (D129 Q2; design `docs/design/cls_tree_design.md` §2.2, §6.1). Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only.

<a id="s2-33-p2"></a>[2.33¶2] **Wide classes.** A WIDE class has more than one member and some member that encodes deeper than one code unit; under `-e byte` no class is wide. The VM decodes one character through the encoding's `static inline` `<prefix>_decode` (`match_api.md` §6.3.8¶16) and tests it with `<prefix>_wcls<N>`, a `static inline` matcher, one per distinct set per artifact. The matcher's FORM is λ's row of §5.4 (`src/gen/clskit.c`'s first-match `ROWS`): the sectioned kit `K`, or a whole-set table `P3`, `P2` or `B1`. The decoder rejects a truncated sequence, a stray continuation byte, an overlong form, a surrogate and anything above U+10FFFF — exactly what the byte alternation cannot match — so ill-formed input matches nothing on either route. A one-member wide class is a literal and keeps its bytes. The DFA, the NFA and a hybrid's prefilter always read the byte alternation.

<a id="s2-33-p3"></a>[2.33¶3] **Byte classes.** At `−2`/`−1` a VM byte class that is neither one interval nor an ASCII fold pair, and whose table-read classes do not take §2.34's shared atom table, is tested by `<prefix>_class_kit<N>(byte)`, the same kit's `K` matcher, in place of its 32-byte bitmap — only where the kit is smaller (the `byte-kit` row): the kit's estimate (its model bytes plus a dispatch term fitted per domain) against the table its site reads. At `0`/`+1`/`+2` a byte class keeps its table. A wide class whose set is one interval of code points at or below U+00FF (`[\x{e0}-\x{ff}]` under `-e utf8`) takes the `byte-range` row and is one range compare at every position.

<a id="s2-33-p4"></a>[2.33¶4] **Scan edges.** At `−2`/`−1` a DFA scan edge (§2.18) whose class the same table puts on `byte-kit` — asked at the scan site, against the edge's 256-byte table — tests its run with `<prefix>_<machine>_scankit<N>`, stamped `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "kit"`. A row's flag denies it wherever the class-form table is read (D139), so the edge falls back to its table under this flag.

<a id="s2-33-p5"></a>[2.33¶5] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_KIT`, the number of distinct matchers written (wide-class matchers and byte-class kit matchers), a VM-only activity count: `0` under the flag and in every `-e byte` artifact at `0`/`+1`/`+2`.

<a id="s2-33-p6"></a>[2.33¶6] **Denied**, every wide class on the VM is the byte alternation, every byte class reads its table, every scan edge reads its table, and the shared atom table of §2.34 (a kit form too) is denied with them: every table-read byte class keeps its own bitmap. The artifact accepts exactly the same subjects.

<a id="s2-33-p7"></a>[2.33¶7] **The denial moves the refusal set, by design.** The byte alternation of a large wide class can exceed the emitted-code cap, so under this flag such a pattern is refused on the VM (`--engine=vm`, or a default-route pattern that selects it, such as a capturing `\P{Unknown}`), with `pattern too large: N bytes of emitted code (limit 500000)`. No size-ladder rung applies. `make test-axes` records the refusal as this axis's documented limit.

<a id="s2-34"></a>
### 2.34 `-fno-cls-pack` — `PCREC_NO_CLS_PACK` (bit 38)

<a id="s2-34-p1"></a>[2.34¶1] **Denies** the SHARED ATOM TABLE for a VM program's table-read byte classes (D131 item 6; design `docs/design/cls_tree_design.md` §1.7.3). A byte class reads a table when no compare form covers it: it is not a single byte, a contiguous range or an ASCII fold pair (§2.22). The choice is made once per artifact, by `src/gen/clskit.c`'s first-match `TAB_ROWS`:

| row | deny | predicate | form |
|---|---|---|---|
| `atom` | `-fno-cls-pack`, or `-fno-cls-kit` (§2.33) | at least `atom_min_sites` (11) table-read classes, whose byte partition has at most `atom_max` (64) atoms | one `static const unsigned char <prefix>_class_atoms[256]` (byte to atom), and per class a `static inline int <prefix>_class_atom<N>(unsigned)` that shifts a 64-bit immediate mask by the byte's atom |
| `scan-table` | — | a scan edge's run test | one 256-byte table per edge (§2.18) |
| `site` | — | always | each class keeps its own form: a 32-byte `<prefix>_class_bitmap<N>`, or its kit matcher at `−2`/`−1` |

<a id="s2-34-p2"></a>[2.34¶2] An ATOM is a set of bytes with identical class membership. 11 is where 256 bytes of shared table plus 8 per class undercuts 32 per class; 64 is the mask's width. Both are `clskit.c`'s `PLACE` cells. Every row lists all five `--tune` positions. Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only. It changes `.rodata` (256 bytes in place of `32N`) and each site's test (a call of the class's matcher, one load and one shift); it does not change which classes read a table, what the DFA or the prefilter emit, or any answer.

<a id="s2-34-p3"></a>[2.34¶3] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_VM_CLS_ATOMS`, the shared table's atom count, `0` when the per-class bitmaps are emitted and under the flag (VM-only).

<a id="s2-35"></a>
### 2.35 `-fno-hyb-reseed` — `PCREC_NO_HYB_RESEED` (bit 37)

<a id="s2-35-p1"></a>[2.35¶1] **Denies** the ADAPTIVE retry of a VM hybrid's attempt loop (design `docs/design/hyb_reseed.md`). A hybrid seeds each search from its DFA prefilter. After a failed attempt at a prefilter answer it either STEPS to the next character and attempts there, or RE-SEEDS, asking the prefilter where the next candidate starts. An attempt at a prefilter answer can fail only where the prefilter recognises a larger language than the pattern: an erased lookaround, an erased atomic cut, or the count collapse (§2.17). The choice is a first-match table, axis `hyb-reseed` in `--list-axes` (the retry rows of the start table `cand_rows[]`, `docs/design/start_table.md`):

| # | row | deny | applies | action |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `exact` | — | the prefilter's language is the pattern's own (no cut, no lookaround, no collapse) | the fixed retry: re-seed where an MRL clamp exists (§2.4), else step. A failed attempt at an answer does not arise |
| 2 | `clamped` | — | an MRL clamp exists | the fixed retry, which already re-seeds after every failed attempt; a step block would add attempts that retry skips, so an answer could become a give-up |
| 3 | `anchored` | — | the pattern is start-anchored (the `start_anchor` fact, `<PREFIX>_VM_START`, §2.25) | the fixed retry: the attempt loop's bound returns after the first failed attempt, so no retry runs. `-fno-vm-anchor-bound` empties the fact and the row together |
| 4 | `adaptive-dense` | `-fno-hyb-reseed` | the compile's byte-rate puts the candidate scan's byte set at a mean gap under the crossover below (under `-e byte` with no `--analysis`, the built-in `default` analysis, so a single common byte such as a space qualifies); where no byte-rate applies the rate is the set's cardinality, so a single byte never qualifies and a wide class can | ADAPTIVE, starting inside an armed step block |
| 5 | `adaptive` | `-fno-hyb-reseed` | always | ADAPTIVE, starting with a short step budget |
| 6 | `fixed` | — | always | the fixed retry |

<a id="s2-35-p2"></a>[2.35¶2] **ADAPTIVE** is decided per call, from two locals of the search function; no global and no `rx_ctx` field is involved, so a matcher stays reentrant and one call never changes the next. Each re-seed reads how far the prefilter's answer jumped. A jump shorter than the crossover arms the step block, and a second short jump with the block armed starts it. The block ends in one re-seed, its probe: a short probe starts the next block at double the length, up to a cap; a long jump disarms the block. `adaptive` spends a small step budget before its first re-seed, unarmed; `adaptive-dense` starts inside a cap-length block, armed. The crossover, the first block, the cap and the first budget are calibrated per program class — frameless (`<PREFIX>_VM_FRAMELESS 1`) or framed — and no `--tune` position moves them (calibration harness: `studies/hyb_reseed_cal/`).

<a id="s2-35-p3"></a>[2.35¶3] **ANSWER-IDENTICAL; the give-up surface moves in one direction.** Both arms attempt only positions no match can be skipped past: re-seeding is sound because the prefilter's language contains the pattern's. The step and work budgets are shared across a call's attempts and only attempts charge them (`limits.md` §3.1); an adaptive row is reached only on a clamp-free artifact, where the fixed retry attempted every position after a failure, so an adaptive retry's attempts are a subset of those, in the same order. A call that gave up can therefore answer; a call that answered answers the same. Masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only.

<a id="s2-35-p4"></a>[2.35¶4] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED`, the row that fired, on every hybrid and on no other artifact. Denied, an adaptive hybrid's program is the fixed retry's apart from that line; an `anchored` artifact is identical with and without the flag, stamp included, because its row is undeniable and sits above the two the flag denies.

<a id="s2-36"></a>
### 2.36 `-futf-check` — `PCREC_FORCE_UTF_CHECK` (bit 39)

<a id="s2-36-p1"></a>[2.36¶1] The second CONTRACT axis (design `docs/design/utf_valid_design.md`, D133). It selects which answer a call gives on an ill-formed subject, not which shape finds it.

| | |
|---|---|
| **What it controls** | whether every entry that takes a subject refuses an ill-formed one before any attempt (`match_api.md` §9.4) |
| **Default** | off: invalid-tolerant, an ill-formed sequence matches nothing and is not reported (`PCRE2_MATCH_INVALID_UTF`'s semantics) |
| **Stamp** | `<PREFIX>_UTF_CHECK`: `"off"`, `"whole"` or `"inert"` |
| **Engine-selecting?** | no: the check sits in the entry, before any engine runs, so the DFA, the VM and the hybrid are covered alike |
| **`rx_info.flags`** | kept, except under `byte` |
| **Inert under** | the `byte` encoding, where every byte string is well-formed: no check is emitted, the stamp reads `"inert"`, the bit is masked, and the artifact is byte-identical to one built without the flag |

<a id="s2-36-p2"></a>[2.36¶2] **What it does.** Under `-e utf8`, after the §2.23 guard (or alignment), the call is refused with `PCREC_ERR_UTF` when an ill-formed sequence begins in `[startpos − LB, n)` — PCRE2's own `PCRE2_UTF` contract, with LB PCRE2's `max_lookbehind` fact. `match_api.md` §9.4 states the range, the order and the step-back; `<prefix>_valid_upto` (`match_api.md` §3.1.2) reports the offset on every artifact whatever this flag says. `-futf-check=extent` is reserved and refused by name.

<a id="s2-36-p3"></a>[2.36¶3] **Why it is off.** One O(n) pass per call, which turns a call a prefilter answers sublinearly into a linear one; a find-all loop validates on every call. `match_api.md` §3.1.2 gives the linear idiom: validate once with `<prefix>_valid_upto`, and loop on an artifact built without this flag.

<a id="s2-36-p4"></a>[2.36¶4] **`make test-axes` excludes it from the identity sweep by name**, asserts the exclusion present, and gives it its own arm: on every corpus cell the checking build must give the default answer iff an independent python oracle finds the cell's checked range well-formed, and `PCREC_ERR_UTF` otherwise (the corpus carries ill-formed subjects on purpose). `tests/utfcheck/` is the differential against libpcre2, offsets included, and the byte-inert identity.

<a id="s2-36-p5"></a>[2.36¶5] **Dial:** no cell, GATE 1 (§5.4).

<a id="s2-37"></a>
### 2.37 `-fno-view-edge` — `PCREC_NO_VIEW_EDGE` (bit 42)

<a id="s2-37-p1"></a>[2.37¶1] **Denies** VIEW-TOLERANT scan edges, axis `view-edge` in `--list-axes`. §2.18's pass refuses any chain that touches a `$`/`\Z`/`\z` position view, which leaves the whole-subject form `(?:[a-z]{0,n})\z` (`match_api.md` §3.6) walking its tables once per byte on the forward pass and the reverse one. With this axis on, two refusals are lifted:

1. <a id="s2-37-p2"></a>[2.37¶2] A member may carry an END view (`\z`, and no EOL view) on a machine whose walk ends at the subject's end: the forward search machine and the anchored match-here machine. There the END view is consulted at one position, `n`, where the loop selects it, reads its accept bit and stops. Every member's END view must carry the same accept bit, and a member whose own bit is set while its END view's is clear is refused, because the scan records its own bit at `n` too. The reverse machine steps from its END view (its walk starts at `n`), so this half never applies to it.
2. <a id="s2-37-p3"></a>[2.37¶3] A chain whose head is another state's view target is trimmed, not refused, on any machine: it starts at the head's class successor, if that state's only way in is the head. `(?:[a-z]{0,n})\z`'s reverse machine is the case: its start state reaches the counting chain only through its END view.

<a id="s2-37-p4"></a>[2.37¶4] Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only. No stamp of its own: `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE` leaving `"none"` is what it changes. Denied, the pass is §2.18's without these two lifts. The reverse pass remains on a whole-subject form (§2.19's pinned start cannot apply where the start state accepts only at `n`).

<a id="s2-38"></a>
### 2.38 `-fno-run-overlap` — `PCREC_NO_RUN_OVERLAP` (bit 43)

<a id="s2-38-p1"></a>[2.38¶1] **Denies** the WORD rows of the run compare, on both engines. Every literal-run compare in emitted C — the offset-skip block's run term (§2.30, which is also the run pre-check's compare, §2.28) and the VM's literal runs and island single-child chains (§2.31) — is written by one renderer, pcrec-memory-functions' run compare (`memfn/src/runcmp.c`), through a first-match row table walked live by `--list-axes`, axis `run-overlap`. The flag reaches the kit as its in-emitter deny `MF_D_RUN_OVERLAP` (`docs/design/memfn/integration.md` §14.10). Design: `docs/design/litscan_s4.md` §1.3-§1.5, §2.1.

| row | applies | emits |
|---|---|---|
| `words` | a MASKED run (some position a two-member cube, §2.39) of length 2 or more | the run's natural-width words, the last at offset `L - W`, each `(w(base + o) & w("<K>")) == w("<T>")` with the mask a string literal too, joined by `&&` in offset order; a word whose mask is all `0xff` compares unmasked, one whose mask is all `0x00` is not loaded |
| `overlap` | an exact run of length 3, 5, 6, 7 or 9-15 | two overlapping natural-width words (2, 4 or 8 bytes), the last at offset `L - W`, joined by `&&` in offset order |
| `bytes` | a masked run (the masked domain's fallback) | `((base)[i] & K) == T` per position, joined by `&&`; `K` `0xff` elides the `&` |
| `memcmp` | an exact run (the exact domain's fallback) | `!memcmp(base, "<run>", L)` |

```c
/* L = 6, the masked necessary run (?i)select, row `words` */
(rx_w4(subject + cand) & rx_w4("\337\337\337\337")) == rx_w4("SELE")
    && (rx_w4(subject + cand + 2) & rx_w4("\337\337\337\337")) == rx_w4("LECT")
```

```c
/* L = 5, the run-pinned prefilter's run term for `/user` */
rx_w4(subject + cand) == rx_w4("/use") && rx_w4(subject + cand + 1) == rx_w4("user")
```

<a id="s2-38-p2"></a>[2.38¶2] Each word is loaded by a `static inline uint<8W>_t <prefix>_w<W>(const void *)` helper that is one `memcpy`, and its constant is the same helper applied to a string literal, which gcc and clang fold to an immediate: no integer literal of the target's byte order appears in the text, so the compare is endian-neutral. The helpers are emitted where the artifact writes a word compare, once each, at file scope ahead of their first use. gcc lowers a constant-length `memcmp` to one load and one compare only at L in {1, 2, 4, 8} and to a vector compare at L >= 16 (`docs/dev/memcmp_lowering_study.md` §3); at the other lengths two overlapping words cover the run in two loads.

<a id="s2-38-p3"></a>[2.38¶3] Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL: the words read exactly the run's `L` bytes behind the bounds guard each site already writes, and the step, work and node budgets charge the compare as they charge the `memcmp` (`limits.md` §3.1). Masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only; the deny is the literal-compare kit's row flag (D122 addendum 2). AddressSanitizer instruments each word load.

<a id="s2-38-p4"></a>[2.38¶4] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_RUN_WORDS`, the number of compares the `words` and `overlap` rows write; `0` on every artifact that writes none and under the flag. Denied, every exact run compare is the `memcmp` and every masked one takes the `bytes` row, byte for byte apart from that stamp line.

<a id="s2-38-p5"></a>[2.38¶5] **Dial:** no cell, NOT A RUNG (§5.4).

<a id="s2-39"></a>
### 2.39 `-fno-req-run-fold` — `PCREC_NO_REQ_RUN_FOLD` (bit 44)

<a id="s2-39-p1"></a>[2.39¶1] **Denies** the two-member CUBE positions of §2.28's necessary run, axis `req-run-fold`. A class whose byte set is one cube of at most `PCREC_MAX_REQ_RUN_POS_SET` members is a run position (§2.28): a caseless letter (D23 folds it to a two-member class), `[jk]`, and an alternation's one-bit hull (`frank|fred` to `fr[ae]`). Without it a caseless word contributes nothing to the necessary run, and `(?i)union.*?select.*?from` has no whole-window pre-check. Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only. Design: `docs/design/litscan_s4.md` §2.3.

<a id="s2-39-p2"></a>[2.39¶2] **What the pre-check emits on a masked run.** The run compare's `words` row (§2.38) verifies it masked. Where the scan member is an exact byte the block is the one-`memchr` loop; where it is a pair, the block scans both members, two pending hits leapfrogged inside the block's one guarded loop (`while (pos + maxk < n)`, so no search is made on a window shorter than the run and `memchr(NULL, c, 0)` cannot occur, K27):

```c
static inline size_t rx_reqrun(const unsigned char *subject, size_t n, size_t pos)
{
    size_t ha = 0, hb = 0;
    int fresh = 1;
    while (pos + 5 < n) {
        size_t cand;
        if (fresh || ha < pos + 4) {
            const void *q = memchr(subject + pos + 4, 67, n - pos - 4);
            ha = q ? (size_t)((const unsigned char *)q - subject) : n;
        }
        if (fresh || hb < pos + 4) {
            const void *q = memchr(subject + pos + 4, 99, n - pos - 4);
            hb = q ? (size_t)((const unsigned char *)q - subject) : n;
        }
        fresh = 0;
        cand = ha < hb ? ha : hb;
        if (cand >= n) return n;
        cand -= 4;
        if (cand + 5 >= n) return n;
        if (/* the masked run compare */) return cand;
        pos = cand + 1;
    }
    return n;
}
```

<a id="s2-39-p3"></a>[2.39¶3] **What it changes for each consumer.** On a DFA artifact and a VM hybrid, a pre-check that does not run, or a one-pass proof of absence: no answer moves. On a VM route with no DFA scan it can only turn a step give-up into a no-match, by running fewer attempts, never the reverse: §2.29's whole-set half keeps testing every set member the run does not prove. `<PREFIX>_REQ_BYTE` stays a set member or `"none"` (§2.27); `<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY "none"` requires no run as well (§2.29); the pin stays a fact about exact positions (§2.30). The activity record is `<PREFIX>_REQ_RUN`'s `/mask` suffix, which only a masked run carries.

<a id="s2-39-p4"></a>[2.39¶4] **Facts narrowed, not emptied** (`--emit-facts`, `docs/spec/facts_listing.md`): `req_whole_run`, `req_run` (and through them `req_byte` and `run_pin`). A fact-level deny (D126 Q3): the walk's position bound drops to one member, so the analysis is the exact-byte one — single bytes ranked by length, an alternation's affixes by byte equality — for every consumer at once.

<a id="s2-39-p5"></a>[2.39¶5] **Dial:** no cell, NOT A RUNG (§5.4).

<a id="s2-40"></a>
### 2.40 `-fno-req-set-lead` — `PCREC_NO_REQ_SET_LEAD` (bit 45)

<a id="s2-40-p1"></a>[2.40¶1] **Denies** the `set-leads` row of §2.29's admission table. A run pre-check (§2.28) rejects a window that lacks the run, and costs one compare per occurrence of its scan member. Where a byte of the necessary SET is rarer than that scan member, a window lacking that byte holds no match either. So where the run pre-check is admitted (no earlier row of §2.29 applies) and the set's pick (§2.27) is strictly rarer than the run's scan member, the artifact emits the set pick's one-byte check first and the run search after it. Rarer is one PICK (`findings.md` §4) over the two guards, the run's scan cube first, so a tie keeps the run alone: under a byte-rate, the set pick's rate against the scan cube's summed rate; with none, the uniform answer, so a byte leads a two-member pair and never an exact byte. On the no-DFA-scan VM route §2.29's whole-set half then skips the byte the lead already tested. `wild-secrets-username-password-pair` (`(?:username|USERNAME|user|USER)[ \t]*=…`) is the witness: `=` is tested first and a subject without it returns after one `memchr`.

<a id="s2-40-p2"></a>[2.40¶2] Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only. `<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY` reads `"emitted"` either way, so the activity record is the emitted text (`--list-axes` axis `req-admit`, row `set-leads`). Denied, the run pre-check alone.

<a id="s2-40-p3"></a>[2.40¶3] **Dial:** no cell, NOT A RUNG (§5.4).

<a id="s2-41"></a>
### 2.41 `-fno-req-handoff` — `PCREC_NO_REQ_HANDOFF` (bit 46)

<a id="s2-41-p1"></a>[2.41¶1] **Denies** the `handoff` row of the pre-check's USE table, axis `req-use` in `--list-axes` (the first rows of the start table `cand_rows[]`): what a search body does with an emitted run pre-check's answer (design `docs/design/litscan_k82h.md`). A run pre-check finds the least position `c >= startpos` at which the run's window occurs. Every match begins at most `K` bytes before an occurrence of the window, where `K` is the window's maximum byte offset from the attempt start — the core fact `req_run_maxoff` (`facts_listing.md`), counted in bytes on the encoding-lowered pattern (`(?i)straße` under `-e utf8` has `K = 2`: `(?i)s` matches U+017F, two bytes). So no match begins in `[startpos, c − K)`, and the body may begin its scan at `max(startpos, c − K)` and answer exactly what it answers from `startpos`. Denied, the body discards `c` and scans from `startpos`.

<a id="s2-41-p2"></a>[2.41¶2] The row applies where, in order:

- <a id="s2-41-p3"></a>[2.41¶3] the admission (§2.29) emitted a run pre-check — the row calls the admission, so `req-admit`'s verdict reaches it unchanged;
- <a id="s2-41-p4"></a>[2.41¶4] a DFA scan is in front of the body: a DFA artifact (its unanchored scan, whose forward seed reads the byte before the moved start, or its attempt loop's first start), or a VM hybrid, whose first prefilter call starts there; a VM artifact with no DFA scan never takes it;
- <a id="s2-41-p5"></a>[2.41¶5] `K` is finite (`req_run_maxoff` is not `unbounded`);
- <a id="s2-41-p6"></a>[2.41¶6] the hybrid's prefilter is not count-collapsed: its answers may sit below `c − K`, so there the handoff could move a budget-limited search from a give-up to a match;
- <a id="s2-41-p7"></a>[2.41¶7] and the artifact is not a VM hybrid whose program has a `\G` start family and whose prefilter span end is its match ceiling (`<PREFIX>_VM_PRUNE_CEILING "prefilter-window"`).

<a id="s2-41-p8"></a>[2.41¶8] Under a multibyte encoding a moved start is rounded up to the next character start, through the encoding backend's start predicate and bounded only by the subject's end; a start that did not move is used as the caller gave it, so `-fno-startpos-guard`'s semantics are unchanged. `\G` keeps asserting at `startpos`, and the DFA's reverse pass keeps `startpos` as its lower bound.

<a id="s2-41-p9"></a>[2.41¶9] Default: on. ANSWER-IDENTICAL and give-up-preserving: the excluded rows above are the ones where the move could change a give-up. Masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only. **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_REQ_HANDOFF`, the `K` or `"none"`, on every artifact; `"none"` under the flag.

<a id="s2-41-p10"></a>[2.41¶10] **Dial:** no cell, NOT A RUNG (§5.4).

<a id="s2-42"></a>
### 2.42 `-fno-start-set` — `PCREC_NO_START_SET` (bit 47)

<a id="s2-42-p1"></a>[2.42¶1] **Denies** the candidate table's START-SET rows (design `docs/design/startset.md`, D148): the VM-route row `first-class` and the DFA-route rows `first-memchr-bounded` and `first-class-bounded`, all on the `prefilter` axis of `--list-axes`. Default: on. Masked out of `rx_info.flags`. Deny-only. Both halves read the `start_set` fact (`facts_listing.md`): the first byte of every non-empty match, with every zero-width construct erased, on the encoding-lowered pattern (so under `-e utf8` it holds lead bytes).

<a id="s2-42-p2"></a>[2.42¶2] **The VM half.** A VM artifact with no DFA prefilter starts an attempt at every position from `startpos`. Where the pattern cannot match empty, the attempt loop seeks the next byte of the start set `S` before its first attempt and after each failed one (after the encoding's own advance), and answers no-match when none is left. The row applies where the artifact is a VM artifact with no DFA prefilter (`<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "none"`, at `auto` or under `--engine=vm`); the pattern is unanchored (`start_anchor`); and `S` is not nullable and has fewer than 256 members. The seek is a 256-entry table walk at any size of `S`. It sits after the range guard, the startpos guard, `-futf-check`'s subject check and the whole-set and whole-run pre-checks, so none of their answers move; `\G` keeps asserting at `startpos`. **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_VM_START_SCAN`, `"first-class"` or `"none"`, on every artifact.

<a id="s2-42-p3"></a>[2.42¶3] **The VM half is ANSWER-IDENTICAL and not give-up-preserving, in one direction.** A skipped attempt spends no steps, work, backtrack frames or trail, so a search that gives up under the flag may return, with it, the answer an unbounded budget returns (`match_api.md` §3.1): `(?=(?:a|b|x)*c)x` under `--engine=vm --backtrack-frames=8` on `(ab)×12` + `"xc"` gives up `PCREC_ERR_FRAMES` denied and answers `(24,25)` with the row (`tests/startset/giveup.rxt`).

<a id="s2-42-p4"></a>[2.42¶4] **The DFA half.** The forward scan skips, while it sits in its start state with nothing found, over bytes that cannot move it: the start state's ESCAPE set `E`. On a SEEDED machine — one whose start depends on the byte before it (`\b`, `\B`, a lookbehind, a `(?m)` context) — `E` holds every byte that changes that context, not only the bytes a match can begin with (`\b(?:true|false|null)\b`'s `E` is the 63 word bytes, where only `t`, `f` and `n` start a match). The rows skip over the start set `T = S` instead and, where the skip moved, re-seed the scan state from the byte before the landing, as a search started there would. They apply to the unanchored forward scan (a DFA artifact, or a hybrid's inlined prefilter) of a seeded machine whose plain skip they replace (`byte-class-bounded`; the offset and run rows sit above them), with `S` not nullable and under 256 members, and `T` a non-empty proper subset of `E`. A start byte outside `E` fails that test and the plain row ships, so the skip never passes a byte a match can begin with. One byte takes `first-memchr-bounded` (a `memchr`), several take `first-class-bounded` (a `<prefix>_start_bytes` table); both are bounded at `n - 1`. ANSWER-IDENTICAL and give-up-preserving: the DFA scan's own steps are not metered. **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER`.

<a id="s2-42-p5"></a>[2.42¶5] Three selections that read the scanned set see `T` where they saw `E`: the dominance test (`<PREFIX>_REQ_WHY` may read `"dominated"` where a one-byte `T` is the pre-check's byte), the hybrid re-seed table (`<PREFIX>_VM_RESEED`, whose density reads the scanned set) and the scan edge (whose precondition reads whether the prefilter re-seeds).

<a id="s2-42-p6"></a>[2.42¶6] **Denied**, every position is attempted on the VM route, and the DFA route takes the plain `byte-class-bounded` skip over `E`.

<a id="s2-42-p7"></a>[2.42¶7] **Dial:** no cell, NOT A RUNG (§5.4).

<a id="s2-43"></a>
### 2.43 `-fno-memfn-simd` / `-fmemfn-simd` — `PCREC_NO_MEMFN_SIMD` (bit 48), `PCREC_FORCE_MEMFN_SIMD` (bit 49)

<a id="s2-43-p1"></a>[2.43¶1] **Controls** whether the memory-function kit (`memfn/`, D147) may render hardware-specific forms. pcrec's one axis for the kit. A force pair, default OFF; the deny spelling states the default and, passed with the force, wins.

- <a id="s2-43-p2"></a>[2.43¶2] **Off (the default):** the kit renders portable C only (plain C, SWAR on ordinary integers, libc calls, loop-free forms), and the artifact runs on any target.
- <a id="s2-43-p3"></a>[2.43¶3] **On:** the kit may render hardware-optimized forms for a specific CPU, and such an artifact may not execute elsewhere. What it renders, which ISA levels and whether it dispatches at run time is the kit's choice per site. pcrec sends the kit one bit, `MF_P_PORTABLE_ONLY`, set iff the force flag is not in force (`pcrec_memfn_policy`, `src/gen/memfn_stamps.c`), and carries no ISA axis of its own.

<a id="s2-43-p4"></a>[2.43¶4] Inert in this build: no SIMD form exists, so `-fmemfn-simd` and `-fno-memfn-simd` produce byte-identical artifacts (checked by `make test-memfn-stamps`, which compiles sampled artifacts under each flag against the default). The kit's per-form switches are its own `--memfn=` namespace (`registry.md` §6, `cli.md` §1.16), not this axis. ANSWER-IDENTICAL. Both bits are masked out of `rx_info.flags`. **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_MEMFN_FORMS` (`match_api.md` §6.3), `"none"` iff the artifact is identical to its SIMD-off compile. SIMD-guarded bytes are excluded from the size caps and from `<PREFIX>_VM_PROGRAM_BYTES` (`limits.md` §8.3).

<a id="s2-44"></a>
### 2.44 `-fno-poss-ctx-follow` — `PCREC_NO_POSS_CTX_FOLLOW` (bit 50)

<a id="s2-44-p1"></a>[2.44¶1] **Denies** possessify's ARM A (design `docs/design/poss_arms.md` §2): a context gate — `\b`, `\B`, or a one-character lookaround (§2.32's context node) — in a quantifier's follow is valued by the next characters it can admit, instead of widening the follow to every byte. One bit, two halves: A0 (nothing known on the gate's left, so it narrows only a lookahead-born gate: `[A-Za-z0-9.]+(?=@)`) and A1 (the left is the loop's own last characters, so `\w+\b` and `(?:a\.)+\B` possessify; greedy loops with at least one mandatory iteration only). Default: both run. Each changes no answer.

<a id="s2-44-p2"></a>[2.44¶2] ENGINE-SELECTING, KEPT in `rx_info.flags`. The free discharge (§2.8) asks the same verdict, so the arm can delete an atomic group or possessive suffix and move a pattern to the DFA; denied, the group stays on the VM, and `--engine=dfa` with the denial refuses (`\w++\b` with `--features all`: `possessive quantifier requires the VM engine, which --engine=dfa excludes`; without the flag it compiles to `RX_ENGINE "dfa"`).

<a id="s2-44-p3"></a>[2.44¶3] **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_VM_POSS_ARMS` bits `0x1` (A0) and `0x2` (A1) (`match_api.md` §6.3), both `0` under the denial (`tests/possessify/run_possessify_tests.sh` asserts it). **Differential:** `tests/possessify/run_possdiff.sh`, denied against armed.

<a id="s2-45"></a>
### 2.45 `-fno-poss-bref-first` — `PCREC_NO_POSS_BREF_FIRST` (bit 51)

<a id="s2-45-p1"></a>[2.45¶1] **Denies** possessify's ARM B (design `docs/design/poss_arms.md` §3): a backreference's first character is read from its groups — the union, over every group number it can name, of the first character of the text each such group can capture, folded where the reference is caseless — instead of every byte. So `\s+` before `\1` in `\b(\w+)\b\s+\1\b` possessifies. Default: it runs.

<a id="s2-45-p2"></a>[2.45¶2] ANSWER-IDENTICAL, masked out of `rx_info.flags`. A backreference is VM-only (under `--no-captures` too), so the arm can change the program and the free discharge but never `<PREFIX>_ENGINE`; `--engine=dfa` refuses a backreference pattern with and without it. `tests/reject/`'s `reject_engine_dfa_bref_nocaptures` holds that premise: if a backreference ever becomes DFA-runnable, this axis becomes engine-selecting. **The stamp** is `<PREFIX>_VM_POSS_ARMS` bit `0x4`, `0` under the denial. **Differential:** `tests/possessify/run_possdiff.sh`.

<a id="s3"></a>
## 3. The DFA scan's stamps

<a id="s3-p1"></a>[3¶1] A DFA artifact carries selection stamps for its scan, in the same place a VM artifact carries its own. `match_api.md` §6.3.4 is their contract (value sets and the conditions each appears under); this section names the axis that governs each:

| stamp | names | axis | `rx_info` mirror |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN` | the scan shape: `"unanchored"` (the O(n) forward scan, followed by a reverse pass that recovers the match start unless `RX_DFA_START` is `"pinned"`), `"attempt"` (the per-start computed-goto loop a `^`/`\A`-bearing pattern takes) or `"empty"` (the pattern provably matches nothing) | none: the engine's own selection | `rx_info.scan` |
| `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER` | the candidate-start mechanism | §2.14, §2.30, §2.42; the plain forms have no flag | `rx_info.prefilter` |
| `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS` | the offsets an `offset-set` or `run-pinned` filter tests | §2.14, §2.30 | none |
| `<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE` | the transition tables' encoding | §2.13 | none |
| `<PREFIX>_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS` | how many of the artifact's DFA tables had all cells equal and are not emitted, their accessor returning the constant | none: what the machine turned out to contain, not a choice | none |
| `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE` | the scan edges' run test | §2.18, §2.22, §2.33, §2.37 | none |
| `<PREFIX>_DFA_START` | how the search recovers the match start: `"pinned"`, `"reverse-pass"`, or `"attempt-start"` (none recovered) | §2.19 | `rx_info.search_form` |
| `<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH` | which form `<prefix>_match` takes: `"unwrapped"` or `"search-filter"` | §2.15 | `rx_info.match_form` |

<a id="s3-p2"></a>[3¶2] A stamp has an `rx_info` mirror where it is a caller-visible cost property of an entry the caller calls (`DFA_MATCH`, `DFA_START`) or where a header-less consumer buckets on it (`DFA_SCAN`, `DFA_PREFILTER`); an internal encoding choice has none (`DFA_TABLE`, `DFA_SCAN_EDGE`, `DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS`, `DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS`). `<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE` names the encoding selected even where every table of it folded, because the encoding fixes the folded constant.

<a id="s3-p3"></a>[3¶3] `<PREFIX>_ENGINE` is unconditional: present on every artifact of both engines, `"vm"` or `"dfa"`, from one emitter. `<PREFIX>_ENGINE_WHY` is VM-only: it names the construct that forced the VM, and a DFA artifact was not forced (`rx_info.engine_why` is `NULL` there). `<PREFIX>_TUNE` (§5.3) belongs to neither engine and is on every artifact.

<a id="s3-1"></a>
### 3.1 A VM hybrid carries the scan's stamps

<a id="s3-1-p1"></a>[3.1¶1] The stamps belong to the mechanism, not to the artifact kind. A VM HYBRID is a VM artifact whose prefilter is on (§2.5): it inlines the DFA emitter's own scan as a `static` function and runs it ahead of the program, tables, bound and candidate-start filter included, so it carries `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN`, `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER`, `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS`, `<PREFIX>_DFA_TABLE`, `<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN_EDGE` and `<PREFIX>_DFA_START`:

```
$ build/pcrec -p rx -o - --pattern 'a(b|c)+d' | grep -E '^#define RX_(ENGINE |VM_PREFILTER |DFA_)'
#define RX_ENGINE "vm"
#define RX_VM_PREFILTER "hybrid"
#define RX_DFA_SCAN "unanchored"
#define RX_DFA_PREFILTER "memchr"
#define RX_DFA_PREFILTER_OFFSETS "none"
#define RX_DFA_TABLE "premultiplied"
#define RX_DFA_UNIFORM_FOLDS 0
#define RX_DFA_SCAN_EDGE "none"
#define RX_DFA_START "reverse-pass"
```

<a id="s3-1-p2"></a>[3.1¶2] `<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH` is the one DFA stamp a hybrid does not carry: it describes the artifact's `<prefix>_match` entry, and a hybrid's is the VM's own anchored body. Its iff is `<PREFIX>_ENGINE "dfa"`, and `rx_info.match_form` is `NULL` on a hybrid where `rx_info.scan` is not.

<a id="s3-1-p3"></a>[3.1¶3] The two prefilter stamps are two different selections: `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER` says whether the VM runs a DFA ahead of its program at all (§2.5), and `<PREFIX>_DFA_PREFILTER` says what candidate-start filter that DFA carries. A VM artifact that is not a hybrid carries no `<PREFIX>_DFA_*` stamp; the relation is an iff (`match_api.md` §6.3).

<a id="s3-2"></a>
### 3.2 `rx_info` carries the same facts at run time

<a id="s3-2-p1"></a>[3.2¶1] The macros are preprocessor-only, so a header-less consumer — a harness that `dlopen`s an artifact, an FFI binding, a tool walking several `<prefix>_info` symbols — reads the mirrors instead: `rx_info.scan` (`<PREFIX>_DFA_SCAN`, or `NULL`), `rx_info.prefilter` (the candidate-start mechanism; never `NULL`), `rx_info.match_form` (`<PREFIX>_DFA_MATCH`, `NULL` on a VM artifact) and `rx_info.search_form` (`<PREFIX>_DFA_START`, non-`NULL` on a DFA artifact and on a hybrid, `NULL` on a plain VM artifact). Each is written from the same emitter derivation as its macro, never a second computation. A non-`NULL` `scan` on a VM artifact is "this is a hybrid", the run-time reading of `<PREFIX>_VM_PREFILTER "hybrid"`; `prefilter` reads the DFA's vocabulary wherever `scan` is non-`NULL` and `"none"` where it is not. `match_api.md` §6 is the field-by-field contract.

<a id="s3-2-p2"></a>[3.2¶2] None of these is a `-f` axis: they observe selections the compiler makes on its own (D46), with no knob to deny or force. `tests/codegen/run_dfa_stamps.sh` holds each stamp to the loop it names (every verdict derived from the emitted matcher text, then compared with the macro), asserts field equals macro on every compiled artifact of both engines, and asserts the hybrid iff in both directions; `tests/codegen/run_search_pinned.sh` does the same for `search_form`, including the `NULL` case.

<a id="s4"></a>
## 4. `pcrec_options` mirror

<a id="s4-p1"></a>[4¶1] Which `pcrec_options` fields (`lib/pcrec.h`) correspond to which axes. `match_api.md` §8.2 states the struct itself; this table maps field to axis, and is exhaustive over `flags`: every bit appears below, either as an axis row or in the list after the table.

| `pcrec_options` field | CLI spelling | axis |
|---|---|---|
| `flags` bit `PCREC_NO_POSSESSIFY` | `-fno-possessify` | §2.1 |
| `flags` bit `PCREC_NO_REVDET` | `-fno-revdet` | §2.2 |
| `flags` bit `PCREC_NO_COUNTER` | `-fno-counter` | §2.3 |
| `flags` bit `PCREC_NO_LENGTH_PRUNE` | `-fno-length-prune` | §2.4 |
| `flags` bits `PCREC_NO_PREFILTER` / `PCREC_FORCE_PREFILTER` | `-fno-prefilter` / `-fprefilter` | §2.5 |
| `flags` bit `PCREC_NO_ALTCLS_MERGE` | `-fno-altcls-merge` | §2.6 |
| `flags` bit `PCREC_NO_ALTCLS_FACTOR` | `-fno-altcls-factor` | §2.7 |

<a id="s4-p2"></a>[4¶2] **The `flags` bits that are not tuning axes:** `PCREC_CASELESS`, `PCREC_EMIT_MAIN` and `PCREC_NO_CAPTURES` are semantic and output options (`match_api.md` §8.2, `cli.md`); `PCREC_UCP` (`--ucp`) is a semantic axis — it changes what `\d`, `\s`, `\w` and the POSIX classes match, so it is reflected in `rx_info.flags` unmasked, no `--tune` position sets it, and `make test-axes` does not sweep it (`cli.md` §1.9); `PCREC_TRACE` (`--trace`) selects an instrumented matcher that writes an event stream to stderr, which changes what the artifact does at run time (`table_contract.md` §1¶3); and `PCREC_SIZE_CAP_REFUSE` (`--size-cap=refuse`) decides only whether a slower artifact that fits ships or the compile refuses (`limits.md` §8.4), and is masked out of `rx_info.flags`.

<a id="s4-p3"></a>[4¶3] `step_budget`, `work_budget` and `frame_capacity` are resource bounds, not strategy selections, and so are the `max_*` caps and `warn_emit_bytes`: `limits.md` is their home.

<a id="s4-p4"></a>[4¶4] `tune` has no "was it set" bit: an explicitly typed `--tune=balanced` and no flag are the same field value, as `--engine=auto` and no flag are. That is enough for `tune`, because the file-wins rule (§5.1) treats the two alike.

<a id="s5"></a>
## 5. The `--tune` dial

<a id="s5-p1"></a>[5¶1] This section is the dial's contract (D103; the design is `docs/design/opt_dial_design.md`, background only). §5.4's table is PINNED: a cell changes only by an explicit diff to this section, never because a measurement lands. `src/core/tune.c` holds the compiler's copy; `tests/codegen/run_tune_dial.sh` reads its expected values from §5.4's table here, not from `tune.c`, so the check does not share a source with the compiler it checks.

<a id="s5-1"></a>
### 5.1 The five positions

<a id="s5-1-p1"></a>[5.1¶1] `--tune=N`, an ordinal `N` in `-2..+2` with `0` the default, or one of five aliases accepted on equal terms (`src/core/tune.c` owns both spellings):

| N | alias | direction |
|---|---|---|
| −2 | `min-size` | the smallest artifact the measured rates justify |
| −1 | `size` | size-leaning |
| 0 | `balanced` | the defaults, unchanged byte for byte |
| +1 | `speed` | speed-leaning |
| +2 | `max-speed` | the fastest the measured rates justify |

<a id="s5-1-p2"></a>[5.1¶2] A negative value needs the `=` form: `--tune -2` is refused by name, naming `--tune=-2`, because a look-ahead that guessed would make `--tune -o out.c` mean something nobody typed. The aliases have no leading dash. Out of range is refused, never clamped.

<a id="s5-1-p3"></a>[5.1¶3] A `tune` line in a `.rxt` `config` or `target` block takes the same vocabulary, and the file wins: `tune` is not an exception to the file-wins rule (`cli.md` §1.1.4). A conflict between an explicit non-default `--tune=` on the command line and the file's `tune` row is reported on stderr, non-fatally, naming both sources and both values, and the file's value is used:

```
pcrec: FILE:LINE: target 'PREFIX': CLI --tune=min-size and this file's
`tune speed` disagree; using the file's value (--tune is not the
--engine exception)
```

<a id="s5-1-p4"></a>[5.1¶4] There is no `--force-tune`.

<a id="s5-2"></a>
### 5.2 Sign and unit conventions

<a id="s5-2-p1"></a>[5.2¶1] The design's measurements behind §5.4 are stated in one of two quantities:

- <a id="s5-2-p2"></a>[5.2¶2] **`σ`, size**, as a fraction of the default artifact: `σ = 1 − bytes(denied) / bytes(default)`, the median over the switch's own movers, on comment-excluded emitted C bytes. `σ > 0` means the optimization costs those bytes; `σ < 0` means denying it costs bytes ("wrong-signed").
- <a id="s5-2-p3"></a>[5.2¶3] **`m`, time**, as a multiplicative slowdown of end-to-end match time: `m = time(denied) / time(default)`. `m > 1` means denying the switch is slower.

<a id="s5-2-p4"></a>[5.2¶4] A bound (`x₁`, `x₂`, `t_mid`) or a floor (`s`) is an `m` value; a savings floor (`y`, `z_mid`) or a whole-artifact size budget (`Z₁`, `Z₂`) is a `σ` fraction or an artifact multiple. Where a penalty is a distribution over named subject populations, a cell is admitted at its worst measured population, never at its median: a dial position is a promise to a caller who does not choose their subjects.

<a id="s5-3"></a>
### 5.3 The stamp

<a id="s5-3-p1"></a>[5.3¶1] `<PREFIX>_TUNE`, a closed five-token string — the alias, never the number — on every artifact of both engines, in the shared prologue, including at `balanced`:

```c
#define RX_TUNE "balanced"
```

<a id="s5-3-p2"></a>[5.3¶2] A consumer buckets on the token; a number would invite arithmetic on an ordinal. There is no `rx_info` mirror: nothing at run time behaves differently because of the dial. `tune` is not in `rx_info.flags`, which reflects option bits only.

<a id="s5-4"></a>
### 5.4 The policy table

<a id="s5-4-p1"></a>[5.4¶1] One row per axis or parameter the dial may set, and one per axis it is excluded from with its reason. An axis with no row has no dial cell at any position.

<a id="s5-4-p2"></a>[5.4¶2] A cell is a value, or an em-dash: the dial does not touch this axis at this position. A `0`-column cell states the default; every other column states what the dial changes, and a cell equal to the default is an em-dash. `†` marks a cell that is an em-dash pending an unmeasured quantity named in the "why" column; it becomes a cell only by its own diff to this table, never when the measurement lands.

| axis | −2 `min-size` | −1 `size` | 0 `balanced` | +1 `speed` | +2 `max-speed` | why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| λ (class-matcher kit) | smaller of `K`, `P3` | = `−2` | **`P3`** if `K` ≥ 16 sections and `P3` ≤ 1.26×`K`, else `K` | — | smaller of `P2`, `B1` where `0` chose `P3`, else as `0` | the VM's wide-class matcher form (§2.33): one kit constant (λ = 4, the sectioning's size end, `K`) at every position plus a first-match row over the whole-set tables `P3`/`P2`/`B1` (`src/gen/clskit.c` `ROWS`; D131; calibration `docs/design/cls_tree_design.md` §1.7). BYTE classes: a one-interval set is one inline compare and an ASCII fold pair the §2.22 fold compare at every position on the VM (at `−2`/`−1` only on a scan edge); any other byte class reads its kit matcher at `−2`/`−1` where it is smaller than the table its site reads, and a table otherwise (§2.33, §2.34). The same table serves the VM and the scan edge (§2.18) |
| `[ART-SIZE]` ladder — bar | **0.95** | **0.85** | **0.75** | — | — | §2.16 (`PCREC_SIZE_TERM_BAR`); the speed it would buy is below the speed floor `s` |
| `[ART-SIZE]` ladder — threshold | **40,000** | **80,000** | **120,000** | — | — | §2.16 (`PCREC_SIZE_TERM_THRESHOLD`) |
| `-fno-premul-table` | **deny** | — `†` | **allow** | — | — | §2.13; `−2` holds for every share of scan time; `−1` pending the scan-time share `φ_scan` |
| `-fno-anchored-dfa` | — (excluded `†`) | — | **allow** | — | — | §2.15; its worst measured population exceeds the bound `x₂`; pending its own A/B on the shipped flag |
| `-fno-tiered-entry` | — `†` | — `†` | **allow** | — | — | §2.12; pending the entry-time share `φ_entry` |
| `--vm-entry-shape` term | — | — | **4,096** | **8,192** | **8,192** (= `+1`) | §2.21 (`VM_INLINE_CHAIN_MAX_BYTES`); 8,192 covers the measured cheap band, and nothing above it is measured |
| `--unroll=K` | — | — | — | — | — | NOT A RUNG: set by the ladder rows above, never directly (§2.10) |
| `-fno-offset-skip` | — | — | **allow** | — | — | §2.14; flat: below the materiality bar `y` |
| `-fno-scan-edge` | — | — | **allow** | — | — | §2.18; flat: no size fraction to compare against `y` |
| `-fno-altcls-merge` | — | — | **allow** | — | — | §2.6; wrong-signed, and GATE 2 |
| `-fno-altcls-factor` | — | — | **allow** | — | — | §2.7; wrong-signed |
| `--engine` | — | — | **auto** | — | — | §2.11; GATE 5 and GATE 2 (`--engine=dfa` refuses a pattern with captures) |
| `-fno-possessify` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.1; GATE 3: size wrong-signed, time unmeasured |
| `-fno-revdet` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.2; GATE 3: size a wash, time unmeasured |
| `-fno-prefilter` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.5; GATE 3: measured only through an engine-changing proxy |
| `-fno-atomic-discharge` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.8; GATE 3; it moves engine selection |
| `-fno-splice-calls` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.9; GATE 4 |
| `-fno-prefilter-collapse` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.17; GATE 4 |
| `-fno-counter` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.3; NOT A RUNG: a correctness floor |
| `-fno-length-prune` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.4; NOT A RUNG: trades nothing |
| `-fno-start-pinned` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.19; PURE WIN |
| `-fno-alt-island` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.20; PURE WIN |
| `-fno-cls-fold` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.22; NOT A RUNG: absorbed into λ |
| `-fno-startpos-guard` / `-fstartpos-guard=align` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.23; GATE 1 |
| `-futf-check` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.36; GATE 1 |
| `-fno-size-term` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.16; NOT A RUNG: the mechanism the two ladder rows parameterise |
| `-fno-run-overlap` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.38; NOT A RUNG: the row and the `memcmp` it replaces are within a word of each other in size |
| `-fno-req-set-lead` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.40; NOT A RUNG: one more `memchr`, not a size/speed trade |
| `-fno-req-handoff` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.41; NOT A RUNG: removes a rescan, not a size/speed trade |
| `-fno-start-set` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.42; NOT A RUNG: removes attempts and scan steps that cannot begin a match |
| `-fno-req-run-fold` | — | — | — | — | — | §2.39; NOT A RUNG: a narrower or wider necessary fact, not a size/speed trade |
| emitted-size caps | — | — | — | — | — | `limits.md` §8; NOT A RUNG: raise-only refusal boundaries; a dial that lowered one would manufacture refusals |

<a id="s5-4-p3"></a>[5.4¶3] The reason codes:

| code | means |
|---|---|
| **PURE WIN** | measured better on both size and time; a position that turned it off would be strictly worse |
| **GATE 1** | answer-changing by design; permanently flat |
| **GATE 2** | its deny arm moves the refusal set |
| **GATE 3** | one of size and time has no number; flat until it does |
| **GATE 4** | the time cost reverses sign with the workload |
| **GATE 5** | the time cost's range is too wide for any size saving |
| **NOT A RUNG** | a floor, a boundary, a no-op, or a parameter of another row |

<a id="s5-4-p4"></a>[5.4¶4] `+2` differs from `+1` only on λ's row. The measurements and the gate arguments behind each row are `docs/design/opt_dial_design.md` §3 and `docs/design/opt_dial_inventory.md`.

<a id="s5-5"></a>
### 5.5 Acceptance

<a id="s5-5-p1"></a>[5.5¶1] The dial's acceptance is answer identity across all five positions over the whole corpus: `make test-axes` sweeps the dial as one more axis, and no position may move the refusal set in either direction. `tests/codegen/run_tune_dial.sh` checks that every position stamps its own token under both spellings, that `balanced` is byte-identical to no flag, and that each moving cell's mechanism state, recovered from the emitted text, is the cell §5.4 states. The check IDs and sabotage rows are `docs/design/opt_dial_design.md` §6 and §8.
